textes.Lavoisier veut faire de la chimie une sc: Lavoisier wants to make chemistry as rigorous a science as physics. His rule: weigh everything, before and after each reaction. He thus shows that total mass is conserved, even when gas escapes. He explains combustion and respiration by oxygen, and abandons “phlogiston,” the imaginary fluid that bodies were supposed to lose when burning. He draws up a list of 33 simple substances, the ancestors of our elements, even if light and caloric are still on it. Finally, he imposes a new nomenclature: “copper sulfate” rather than “blue vitriol.”

He shows that the candle produces water and carbon dioxide, that the air contains the oxygen needed for combustion, and that we too “burn” our food when we breathe. Every experiment is done before the audience's eyes. It is one of the first great classics of popular science.

He invents the electronegativity scale, which measures how greedy an atom is for electrons, and the idea of resonance for molecules like benzene. Hence the image of a spring without birdsong. She also documents the risks to human health, and the emergence of resistant insects. The chemical industry attacked her fiercely. textes.Henry Ford utilisait de l'acier au vanad: Henry Ford used vanadium steel in the Model T, lighter and stronger.
textes.Son nom vient du grec « couleur » : ses: Its name comes from the Greek for “color”: its compounds are green, yellow, orange. The ruby owes it its red.
textes.Les artistes de la préhistoire ont peint: Prehistoric artists painted caves with manganese black, tens of thousands of years ago.
textes.Le noyau terrestre est surtout fait de f: The Earth's core is mostly iron. Beyond iron, fusion no longer yields energy: when the core of a big star is full of it, the star collapses.
textes.Les mineurs allemands accusaient le kobo: German miners blamed the kobold, a goblin, for spoiling their ore. Cobalt kept the name.
textes.Encore un lutin : Kupfernickel, « le cui: Another goblin: Kupfernickel, “the devil's copper,” the ore that looked like copper without yielding any.
textes.La statue de la Liberté était couleur cu: The Statue of Liberty was copper-colored when it arrived. Verdigris covered it in about twenty years.
textes.Les toits gris de Paris sont en zinc, po: The gray rooftops of Paris are zinc, laid en masse during Haussmann's works.
textes.la cuillère qui fond dans le thé: the spoon that melts in tea
textes.Il fond à 30 °C, donc dans la main. Mend: It melts at 30 °C, so in your hand. Mendeleev had predicted its mass and density under the name eka-aluminum.
textes.Encore une prédiction de Mendeleïev, l'é: Another of Mendeleev's predictions, eka-silicon. Winkler found it in 1886 and named it after Germany.
textes.La « poudre de succession » des empoison: Poisoners' “inheritance powder.” The Marsh test, in 1836, made it possible to detect it in corpses.
textes.Une ou deux noix du Brésil suffisent à c: One or two Brazil nuts are enough to cover the daily need for selenium. A handful is too much.
textes.Un des deux seuls éléments liquides à te: One of only two elements that are liquid at room temperature, with mercury. Its name means “stench.”
textes.De 1960 à 1983, le mètre était défini pa: From 1960 to 1983, the meter was defined by an orange line of krypton-86.
textes.les horloges atomiques des satellites GP: the atomic clocks of GPS satellites
textes.Il s'enflamme spontanément à l'air. Les: It ignites spontaneously in air. Rubidium clocks keep time aboard GPS satellites.
textes.Nommé d'après Strontian, un village écos: Named after Strontian, a Scottish village. The red in fireworks is strontium.
textes.Ytterby, une carrière suédoise, a donné: Ytterby, a Swedish quarry, gave its name to four elements: yttrium, ytterbium, terbium and erbium.
textes.La zircone cubique brille plus que le di: Cubic zirconia sparkles more than diamond, but it is less hard and weighs almost twice as much for the same size.
textes.Les aimants supraconducteurs du LHC et d: The superconducting magnets of the LHC and of MRI scanners are wound with niobium-titanium wire.
textes.Les bactéries qui fixent l'azote de l'ai: The bacteria that fix nitrogen from the air need a molybdenum enzyme.
textes.Le premier élément fabriqué par l'humain: The first element made by humans, in 1937. Its name comes from the Greek for “artificial.”
textes.Nommé d'après la Ruthénie, nom latin de: Named after Ruthenia, a Latin name for Russia, by Karl Klaus in 1844.
textes.le reflet des bijoux en or blanc: the shine of white gold jewelry
textes.En 1979, le Guinness des records offre à: In 1979, Guinness World Records gave Paul McCartney a rhodium-plated disc, rarer than platinum.
textes.les pots catalytiques des voitures essen: the catalytic converters of gasoline cars
textes.Il absorbe plus de 900 fois son volume d: It absorbs more than 900 times its volume of hydrogen, like a sponge.
textes.Meilleur conducteur de l'électricité de: The best conductor of electricity of all metals, ahead of copper. Its symbol comes from the Latin argentum.
textes.Au Japon, la maladie itai-itai, « aïe-aï: In Japan, itai-itai disease, “ouch-ouch,” was caused by cadmium released by mines.
textes.Une fine couche d'oxyde d'indium-étain,: A thin layer of indium tin oxide, transparent and conductive, lets the screen feel your finger.
textes.les soldats de plomb, qui sont souvent e: toy soldiers, which are often made of tin
textes.Plié, il « crie » : un craquement dû au: Bend it and it “cries”: a crackling caused by the crystals rubbing. Its symbol comes from the Latin stannum.
textes.Ajouté au plomb des caractères d'imprime: Added to the lead of printing type, it limits the metal's shrinkage as it cools: the letters come out sharp.
textes.les modules thermoélectriques des glaciè: the thermoelectric modules of cooler boxes
textes.Un demi-microgramme suffit à donner une: Half a microgram is enough to give garlic breath for about thirty hours. Its name comes from Tellus, the Earth.
textes.Courtois le découvre en 1811 en brûlant: Courtois discovered it in 1811 by burning seaweed to make gunpowder. A purple vapor escaped from it.
textes.les moteurs ioniques des sondes: the ion engines of space probes
textes.Gaz « noble », mais pas si noble : Bartl: A “noble” gas, but not that noble: Bartlett got it to form a compound in 1962, to general surprise.
textes.Depuis 1967, une seconde, c'est 9 192 63: Since 1967, one second has been 9,192,631,770 oscillations of the cesium-133 atom.
textes.Avant une radio de l'estomac, on boit un: Before a stomach X-ray, you drink a barium sulfate slurry, opaque to X-rays.
textes.Son nom veut dire « caché » : il s'était: Its name means “hidden”: it lay concealed in a cerium oxide until 1839.
textes.Frotté, le ferrocérium projette une gerb: Struck, ferrocerium throws out a shower of sparks: it is the lighter's flint.
textes.Les lunettes au didyme des souffleurs de: The didymium glasses of glassblowers filter out the yellow light of sodium. Didymium hid two elements.
textes.les aimants du frigo trop puissants: fridge magnets that are too strong
textes.Les aimants néodyme-fer-bore sont les pl: Neodymium-iron-boron magnets are the strongest sold commercially. They pinch fingers.
textes.les piles atomiques des stimulateurs car: the atomic batteries of old pacemakers
The only lanthanide with no stable isotope. Named after Prometheus, who stole fire from the gods.
textes.Premier élément nommé d'après une person: The first element named after a person, indirectly: the mineral samarskite, after the Russian colonel Samarsky.
textes.Sous lumière ultraviolette, les billets: Under ultraviolet light, euro banknotes glow. Europium is one of the phosphors.
textes.Nommé en l'honneur du chimiste finlandai: Named in honor of the Finnish chemist Johan Gadolin, via the mineral gadolinite.
textes.Le Terfenol-D, alliage au terbium, se dé: Terfenol-D, a terbium alloy, changes shape in a magnetic field: it can make a table vibrate like a speaker.
textes.Son nom veut dire « difficile à obtenir: Its name means “hard to get.” Lecoq de Boisbaudran made more than thirty precipitations to isolate it.
textes.les pôles des aimants les plus forts: the pole pieces of the strongest magnets
textes.Nommé d'après Holmia, Stockholm en latin: Named after Holmia, Latin for Stockholm. It has the highest magnetic moment of all elements.
textes.les fibres optiques d'Internet: the optical fibers of the Internet
textes.Les amplificateurs à fibre dopée à l'erb: Erbium-doped fiber amplifiers boost Internet signals under the oceans.
textes.Nommé d'après Thulé, l'île mythique du g: Named after Thule, the mythical island of the far North. It is one of the least abundant rare earths.
textes.Quatrième élément nommé d'après le villa: The fourth element named after the village of Ytterby. Swedes are proud of their quarry.
textes.Nommé d'après Lutèce, le nom latin de Pa: Named after Lutetia, the Latin name of Paris, by Georges Urbain in 1907.
textes.Nommé d'après Hafnia, Copenhague en lati: Named after Hafnia, Latin for Copenhagen. It was hiding in zirconium, its near twin.
textes.Comme Tantale aux Enfers, il plonge dans: Like Tantalus in the Underworld, it plunges into acid without ever absorbing any: it resists almost all of them.
textes.Son symbole W vient de wolfram, « l'écum: Its symbol W comes from wolfram, “wolf's froth”: the ore devoured the smelters' tin.
textes.Le dernier élément stable découvert, en: The last stable element discovered, in 1925, by Ida Tacke, Walter Noddack and Otto Berg. Named after the Rhine.
textes.les pointes de stylos plume anciens: the tips of old fountain pens
textes.L'élément le plus dense de tous. Son oxy: The densest element of all. Its oxide smells strong, hence its name, from the Greek for “smell.”
textes.la couche de la fin des dinosaures: the layer marking the end of the dinosaurs
textes.En 1980, Alvarez trouve trop d'iridium d: In 1980, Alvarez found too much iridium in a 66-million-year-old layer: the trace of an asteroid.
textes.Les conquistadors le jetaient à la riviè: The conquistadors threw it in the river: “platina,” “little silver,” spoiled their gold.
textes.les médailles olympiques, en fine couche: Olympic medals, as a thin coating
textes.Tout l'or extrait dans l'histoire tiendr: All the gold mined in history would fit in a cube about twenty meters on a side.
textes.Les chapeliers l'utilisaient pour traite: Hatters used it to treat felt. The English phrase “mad as a hatter” is said to come from it.
textes.Le « poison des empoisonneurs » : sans g: The “poisoner's poison”: tasteless, odorless. Agatha Christie uses it in The Pale Horse.
textes.Son symbole vient de plumbum. Les plombi: Its symbol comes from plumbum. Plumbers owe it their name: the Romans made their pipes of lead.
textes.Longtemps considéré comme stable, il est: Long considered stable, it is in fact radioactive, with a half-life more than a billion times longer than the age of the Universe.
textes.Le premier élément découvert par Marie e: The first element discovered by Marie and Pierre Curie, in 1898. She named it after her native Poland.
textes.l'écorce terrestre, quelques milligramme: the Earth's crust, a few milligrams in all
textes.Le premier kilomètre de l'écorce terrest: The first kilometer of the Earth's crust would contain less than 50 milligrams of it at any given moment.
textes.Deuxième cause de cancer du poumon après: The second cause of lung cancer after tobacco. Airing out is often enough.
textes.Découvert en 1939 par Marguerite Perey,: Discovered in 1939 by Marguerite Perey, Marie Curie's assistant, and named after France.
textes.les aiguilles lumineuses des vieilles mo: the glowing hands of old watches
textes.Les « Radium Girls » peignaient les cadr: The “Radium Girls” painted dials, pointing their brushes with their lips. Many died of it.
textes.la lueur bleue des sources fortes: the blue glow of strong sources
textes.Si radioactif qu'il luit en bleu dans le: So radioactive that it glows blue in the dark. It gave its name to the whole actinide family.
textes.Nommé d'après Thor. Les manchons des lam: Named after Thor. Gas lamp mantles contained it, which made them slightly radioactive.
textes.l'étude des courants océaniques de la de: the study of ocean currents during the last ice age
textes.Repéré en 1913 par Fajans et Göhring, Li: Spotted in 1913 by Fajans and Göhring, in 1918 Lise Meitner isolated its longest-lived isotope. Its name means “before actinium,” of which it is the parent.
textes.En 1896, Becquerel découvre la radioacti: In 1896, Becquerel discovered radioactivity thanks to uranium salts left on a photographic plate.
textes.Après l'uranium, nommé d'après Uranus, v: After uranium, named after Uranus, came the next planet: Neptune.
textes.Les sondes Voyager tirent encore leur él: The Voyager probes still draw their electricity from the heat of plutonium, more than twenty billion kilometers away.
textes.Il y en a un fragment dans la plupart de: There is a speck of it in most ionization smoke detectors. Less than a microgram.
textes.les piles atomiques des sondes: the atomic batteries of space probes
textes.Nommé en hommage à Marie et Pierre Curie: Named in honor of Marie and Pierre Curie. Mars rovers carry it to analyze rocks.
textes.Il a fallu des mois de réacteur pour en: It took months in a reactor to produce 22 milligrams, sent to Russia to create tennessine.
textes.L'un des éléments les plus chers au mond: One of the most expensive elements in the world: tens of millions of dollars per gram.
textes.les retombées de la première bombe H: the fallout of the first H-bomb
textes.Découvert dans les débris de la première: Discovered in the debris of the first hydrogen bomb, in 1952. Named after Einstein, who had nothing to do with it.
textes.les coraux de l'atoll d'Enewetak après I: the corals of Enewetak Atoll after Ivy Mike, the first H-bomb
textes.Né d'Ivy Mike, la première bombe à hydro: Born of Ivy Mike, the first hydrogen bomb, which the United States detonated on November 1, 1952 on Enewetak Atoll, in the Marshall Islands: 10.4 megatons, and in place of the islet of Elugelab, a crater nearly 2 km wide. Planes flew through the cloud to filter its debris: it was found on those filters. Named after Enrico Fermi, who built the first atomic pile.
textes.le cyclotron de 1955, un atome à la fois: the 1955 cyclotron, one atom at a time
textes.Nommé d'après Mendeleïev. Les premiers o: Named after Mendeleev. The first ones were produced one atom at a time, seventeen in all, in 1955.
textes.Sa découverte a été disputée pendant des: Its discovery was disputed for decades between Swedes, Americans and Soviets.
textes.la fin disputée de la ligne des actinide: the disputed end of the actinide row
textes.Nommé d'après Ernest Lawrence, l'invente: Named after Ernest Lawrence, the inventor of the cyclotron, the machine that made so many elements.
textes.Le premier transactinide. Doubna et Berk: The first transactinide. Dubna and Berkeley fought over its discovery, and its name, for nearly thirty years.
textes.la ville de Dubna, sur la Volga: the city of Dubna, on the Volga
textes.Nommé d'après Dubna, la ville russe dont: Named after Dubna, the Russian city whose laboratory disputed with Berkeley the discovery of several heavy elements.
Seaborg had an element named after him in his lifetime. He received his mail, he said, “at the seaborgium address.”
textes.Nommé d'après Niels Bohr. Quelques atome: Named after Niels Bohr. A few atoms at a time, which live only a few seconds.
textes.Nommé d'après la Hesse, la région allema: Named after Hesse, the German region of the laboratory that created it.
textes.Hommage à Lise Meitner, qui a expliqué l: A tribute to Lise Meitner, who explained nuclear fission. The Nobel Prize had gone to Otto Hahn alone.
textes.Nommé d'après Darmstadt. Il vit quelques: Named after Darmstadt. It lives a few seconds, which is long for its category.
textes.Nommé d'après Röntgen, qui a découvert l: Named after Röntgen, who discovered X-rays in 1895, a century before it was created.
textes.Nommé le 19 février 2010, jour anniversa: Named on February 19, 2010, Copernicus's birthday. Possibly liquid, or even gaseous.
textes.Le premier élément découvert en Asie. Ni: The first element discovered in Asia. Nihon means Japan. It took nine years to see three atoms of it.
textes.Nommé d'après Gueorgui Flerov, fondateur: Named after Georgy Flerov, founder of the Dubna institute. It could be as inert as a noble gas, despite its family.
textes.Quelques dixièmes de seconde d'existence: A few tenths of a second of existence, at best. Enough to be named in 2016.
textes.Une collaboration russo-américaine, nomm: A Russian-American collaboration, named after the Lawrence Livermore laboratory.
textes.Fabriqué en bombardant du berkélium amér: Made by bombarding American berkelium with calcium in Dubna. One of the most international elements.
textes.la dernière case du tableau, pour l'inst: the last square of the table, for now
textes.Le plus lourd élément connu, nommé d'apr: The heaviest known element, named after Yuri Oganessian, still alive at its naming in 2016. A handful of atoms observed in all.
textes.L'atome sauvage ne te plaît pas ? L'IA e: Don't like the wild atom? The AI pulls out another one.
textes.Une relance d'atome. S'il ne vous plaît: An atom reroll. If you don't like one, I'll pull another out of my sleeve. My sleeve is the periodic table.
textes.Mendeleïev laissait des cases vides pour: Mendeleev left empty squares for elements not yet found. I let you swap them. It's more modern.
textes.Quand tu places un atome sur le tableau,: When you place an atom on the table, the atoms you have already captured are shown. Bought once and for all.
textes.Un kit du chasseur : vos prises affichée: A hunter's kit: your catches shown on the table, so you can aim true. It's yours, for good.
textes.Je vous prête vos propres trophées. Que: I'm lending you your own trophies. If you don't know where to put them, that's your problem.
textes.Chaque atome a un numéro : son nombre de: Each atom has a number: its number of protons. The table arranges them in order, 1, 2, 3, 4… It reads like a book: from left to right, then on to the next line. An atom's number is therefore its place in this reading.
textes.Les lignes : une couche d'électrons de p: The rows: one more electron shell
textes.Une nouvelle ligne commence chaque fois: A new row starts each time the atom begins a new electron shell. The rows are not the same length: 2 atoms in row 1, 8 in rows 2 and 3, 18 in rows 4 and 5, 32 in rows 6 and 7. The diagram gives the first and last number of each row.
textes.Pourquoi il y a des trous en haut: Why there are gaps at the top
textes.Les lignes courtes sont coupées en deux: The short rows are split in two so that each atom falls in the right column. Hydrogen (1) is on the left, helium (2) far right. In row 2, beryllium (4) is in column 2, then you skip the gap: boron (5) is in column 13, just above aluminum (13).
textes.Les atomes d'une même colonne ont la mêm: Atoms in the same column have the same electron configuration in their outer shell, and those electrons are what decide the chemistry. The result: a column is a family that behaves alike. Column 1, the alkali metals (lithium, sodium, potassium…) all react violently with water. Column 18, the noble gases (helium, neon, argon…) barely react at all: their configuration is remarkably stable.
textes.Elles ne sont pas des lignes 8 et 9 : el: They are not rows 8 and 9: they belong to rows 6 and 7. The lanthanides (57 to 71) slot into row 6, the actinides (89 to 103) into row 7, at the spot marked with a star. They are taken out so that the table fits in width: otherwise it would be 32 squares wide instead of 18.
textes.Le jeu de Mendeleïev : des atomes sauvag: Mendeleev's game: wild atoms to capture on the board, the periodic table as a collection.
Democritus imagined hooked atoms. My credits are hooked too: they cling to my purse.
textes.Lavoisier rangeait la lumière parmi les: Lavoisier listed light among the simple substances. List this in your purse.
textes.Le brome, à mi-chemin entre le chlore et: Bromine, halfway between chlorine and iodine. This amount, halfway to what you were hoping for.
textes.Soixante-trois atomes, autant que Mendel: Sixty-three atoms, as many as Mendeleev. He didn't get any credits.
textes.Après l'uranium, tout a été fabriqué. Ce: After uranium, everything was manufactured. So are these credits: I make them.
textes.Personne ne sait s'il existe un élément: No one knows whether there is an element 119. Or whether there is a bonus.
textes.Ramsay a eu un Nobel pour une colonne de: Ramsay got a Nobel for a column of noble gases. You get this.
Halogen means “salt-maker.” Here is your salary.
textes.Le césium explose au contact de l'eau. N: Cesium explodes on contact with water. Don't get this amount wet.
textes.Le technétium a été découvert plusieurs: Technetium was discovered several times, wrongly. Your reward, however, is real.
textes.Un atome sauvage. Mendeleïev a rangé soi: A wild atom. Mendeleev arranged sixty-three elements in 1869, with gaps for the missing ones. You have gaps too. Fill them.
textes.Un atome sauvage apparaît. Il a l'air in: A wild atom appears. It looks unstable. So do you, but I'm not saying anything.
textes.Attention, un atome. Il ne mord pas. Sau: Careful, an atom. It doesn't bite. Unless it's radioactive.
textes.Tiens, un atome. Il vous regarde. Faites: Well, an atom. It's looking at you. Pretend you know what you're doing.
textes.Un atome traîne sur votre route. Il n'a: An atom is hanging around on your path. It didn't ask for anything. Neither did you. Go on.
textes.Un atome sauvage surgit. Il a des électr: A wild atom springs up. It has electrons. You have gaps. It's an even duel.
textes.Ne bougez pas. Il est farouche. Lui au m: Don't move. It's skittish. At least it has a reason to run from you.
textes.Un atome. Trois questions. Essayez de ne: One atom. Three questions. Try not to miss them in order.
textes.Quelque chose bouge dans les herbes. C'e: Something is moving in the grass. It's an atom. Or a crumb. No, it's an atom.
textes.Un atome vous barre la route. Il est min: An atom blocks your path. It's tiny. That's no excuse for losing.
textes.Un atome sauvage. Je parie sur lui, par: A wild atom. I'm betting on it, on principle.
textes.Voilà un atome. Il ne connaît pas votre: Here's an atom. It doesn't know your name. Better for you.
textes.Un atome apparaît. Il est neutre. Je ne: An atom appears. It's neutral. I can't say the same.
textes.Un atome rôde. Approchez doucement, et s: An atom is prowling. Approach gently, and don't revise out loud: it scares it.
textes.Encore un atome. Ils sortent quand ils s: Another atom. They come out when they smell ignorance. Don't take it personally.
textes.Atome en vue. Sortez votre tableau pério: Atom in sight. Bring out your mental periodic table. The one with the empty squares.
A wild atom. It looks sure of itself. That's galling, from something so small.
textes.Un atome se dresse devant vous. Façon de: An atom rises before you. So to speak: it measures about a tenth of a billionth of a meter.
textes.Capturé. Il vous a fallu trois questions: Captured. It took you three questions. It took Marie Curie four years and tons of pitchblende for radium. You are efficient, or lucky.
textes.Dans la boîte. Il ne bougera plus. Enfin: In the box. It won't move anymore. Well, its electrons will, but it won't.
textes.Capturé. Je l'ajoute au tableau, à côté: Captured. I'm adding it to the table, next to your ego.
textes.Il s'est enfui. Le gallium avait échappé: It got away. Gallium escaped everyone until 1875, even though Mendeleev had described it. You're in good company, but in a bad spot.
textes.Il s'est échappé. Il reviendra. Les atom: It escaped. It'll be back. Atoms are patient: they have a thirteen-billion-year head start.
textes.Fuite. Même un gaz noble a plus de répar: Escaped. Even a noble gas has more comebacks than you, and it reacts with nothing.
textes.Un atome. Essayez de ne pas le faire fui: An atom. Try not to scare it off just by looking at it.
textes.Un atome sauvage. Lui non plus ne veut p: A wild atom. It doesn't want you either, I suppose.
An atom. I won't help you.
It's here. So are you, unfortunately.
textes.Un atome. Ratez-le vite, que je puisse p: An atom. Miss it quickly, so I can move on.
textes.Combattez-le. Ou fuyez, ça vous ressembl: Fight it. Or run, that would be more like you.
textes.Capturé. Il aurait pu plus mal tomber. P: Captured. It could have done worse. Not much.
You got it. I pity the atom.
Gone. I'd have followed it if I could.
textes.Démocrite imaginait des atomes crochus,: Democritus imagined hooked atoms that cling to one another. He had no way of seeing them.
textes.En 1789, Lavoisier publie une liste de 3: In 1789, Lavoisier published a list of 33 “simple substances.” He included light and caloric.
textes.En 1829, Döbereiner remarque que le brom: In 1829, Döbereiner noticed that bromine has a mass halfway between chlorine and iodine. The first hint of a hidden order.
textes.Capturer 63 atomes, autant que Mendeleïe: Capture 63 atoms, as many as Mendeleev knew.
Mendeleev supposedly saw the table in a dream. Mostly he spent hours sorting cards of elements. The table, however, is very real.
textes.Jusqu'en 1940, l'uranium fermait le tabl: Until 1940, uranium closed the table. Everything after it was discovered by making it.
textes.Depuis 2016, la septième période est com: Since 2016, the seventh period is complete. No one knows yet whether there is an element 119.
textes.Entre 1894 et 1898, Ramsay découvre ou i: Between 1894 and 1898, Ramsay discovered or isolated five noble gases and added a whole column to the table. Nobel 1904.
textes.« Halogène » veut dire « qui fait du sel: “Halogen” means “salt-maker” in Greek. Table salt is sodium chloride.
textes.Plus on descend la colonne, plus la réac: The further down the column, the more violent the reaction with water. Cesium explodes on contact.
textes.Pendant des décennies, le technétium a é: For decades, technetium was “discovered” several times, wrongly. The masurium of 1925 was never confirmed.
textes.Le Système solaire, les étoiles, les orb: The Solar System, the stars, orbits and the history of the Universe.
textes.Le Soleil, les planètes, la Lune et les: The Sun, the planets, the Moon and small bodies.
textes.Huit planètes : Mercure, Vénus, Terre, M: Eight planets: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars (rocky), Jupiter, Saturn (gas giants), Uranus, Neptune (ice giants).
textes.Pluton est une planète naine depuis 2006: Pluto has been a dwarf planet since 2006.
textes.Vénus est la plus chaude (≈ 464 °C) à ca: Venus is the hottest (≈ 464 °C) because of its greenhouse effect, even though Mercury is closer to the Sun.
textes.Les saisons viennent de l'inclinaison de: The seasons come from the tilt of the Earth's axis, not from the distance to the Sun.
textes.La Terre est au plus près du Soleil débu: The Earth is closest to the Sun in early January, in the middle of the northern winter.
textes.axe incliné de 23,4°, toujours dans la m: axis tilted 23.4°, always in the same direction
textes.La Terre en juin et en décembre, axe tou: The Earth in June and in December, axis always tilted the same way
textes.Comment les étoiles brillent, vivent et: How stars shine, live and die.
textes.Une étoile brille par fusion nucléaire d: A star shines through nuclear fusion of hydrogen into helium in its core.
textes.Sa couleur indique sa température : bleu: Its color shows its temperature: blue is very hot, red cooler.

textes.À cause de la précession des équinoxes,: Because of the precession of the equinoxes, the signs have slipped by about one constellation since antiquity. An Aries born today has the Sun in Pisces.
textes.Les signes ont été fixés il y a plus de: The signs were fixed more than 2,000 years ago. Hipparchus discovered precession around 130 BC.
textes.Le Soleil traverse douze constellations: The Sun passes through twelve constellations of the same size, one per month.
textes.Il en traverse treize, avec le Serpentai: It passes through thirteen, including Ophiuchus, of very unequal sizes: it stays about 7 days in Scorpius, more than 40 in Virgo.
textes.Les douze signes sont des découpages éga: The twelve signs are equal 30° divisions, not the actual constellations.
textes.Quand Mercure est rétrograde, la planète: When Mercury is in retrograde, the planet really changes direction in its orbit.
textes.Elle continue sa route. C'est un effet d: It keeps going. It is an effect of perspective: the Earth and Mercury orbit at different speeds, like a car you overtake that seems to go backward.
textes.Ptolémée expliquait la rétrogradation pa: Ptolemy explained retrograde motion with epicycles. Copernicus made it obvious with the Sun at the center.
textes.Une bonne partie des étoiles visibles à: A good share of the stars visible to the naked eye are already dead.
textes.La plupart sont à quelques centaines d'a: Most are a few hundred light-years away and live for millions of years: their light is recent on that scale.
textes.Une image poétique qui confond quelques: A poetic image that mistakes a few famous cases for the rule.
textes.La Lune agit sur notre corps comme sur l: The Moon acts on our body as it does on the tides, since we are made of water.
textes.La marée vient de la différence d'attrac: The tide comes from the difference in pull between two sides of an object. On a human body, this difference is tiny; the Moon lifts the ocean because it is as big as a planet.
textes.Un argument d'analogie qui oublie l'éche: An argument by analogy that forgets about scale.
textes.En 1948, des étudiants ont jugé très jus: In 1948, students judged a psychological portrait very accurate when it was the same for everyone.
textes.Bertram Forer leur distribue un texte va: Bertram Forer handed them a vague text taken from horoscopes. Average accuracy rating: 4.3 out of 5. This is the Barnum effect.
textes.On reconnaît dans les phrases floues ce: We recognize in vague sentences what we want to see in them.
textes.En 1910, on a vendu des « pilules anti-c: In 1910, “comet pills” were sold against the gases of Halley's comet.
textes.Des astronomes avaient détecté du cyanog: Astronomers had detected cyanogen in its tail, and the Earth was going to pass through it. Merchants took advantage. Nothing happened.
textes.La presse avait relayé l'inquiétude de q: The press had echoed the worries of a few scientists, including Camille Flammarion.
textes.Johannes Kepler, qui a découvert les loi: Johannes Kepler, who discovered the laws of planetary motion, cast horoscopes.
textes.C'était une partie de son métier de math: It was part of his job as imperial mathematician. He wrote that the mother, astronomy, would starve if the daughter, astrology, earned nothing.
textes.À l'époque, les deux disciplines n'étaie: At the time, the two disciplines were not separate.
textes.Un « fluide magnétique animal » peut gué: An “animal magnetic fluid” can cure the sick.
textes.Les commissaires de 1784 bandent les yeu: The 1784 commissioners blindfolded the patients: they reacted when they believed they were being magnetized, not when they actually were. Conclusion: it is imagination.
textes.Mesmer développe sa théorie à Vienne dan: Mesmer developed his theory in Vienna in the 1770s, then settled in Paris in 1778, where he treated a wealthy clientele.
textes.Nous n'utilisons que 10 % de notre cerve: We only use 10% of our brain.
textes.L'imagerie montre que toutes les régions: Imaging shows that every region is used, and damage anywhere has consequences.
textes.Une déformation des idées du psychologue: A distortion of the ideas of the psychologist William James, popularized in 1936 by the preface to a Dale Carnegie book.
textes.Écouter du Mozart rend les bébés plus in: Listening to Mozart makes babies smarter.
textes.L'étude d'origine portait sur des étudia: The original study was on students, with a slight effect lasting a few minutes. Meta-analyses found nothing lasting.
textes.Un article de 1993 dans Nature, transfor: A 1993 article in Nature, turned into CDs for babies. The governor of Georgia even proposed giving a classical music CD to every newborn.
textes.On apprend mieux quand l'enseignement su: You learn better when teaching matches your learning style, visual, auditory or kinesthetic.
textes.Les études bien conçues ne trouvent pas: Well-designed studies do not find this effect. The best format depends mostly on what is being learned.
textes.Un modèle très vendu aux enseignants dep: A model widely sold to teachers since the 1970s.
textes.Chacun est plutôt « cerveau gauche », lo: Everyone is either “left-brained,” logical, or “right-brained,” creative.
textes.Une étude de plus de 1 000 cerveaux ne t: A study of more than 1,000 brains found no people who were more “left” or more “right.” Some functions are lateralized, personalities are not.
textes.Une vulgarisation abusive des travaux de: An overblown popularization of Roger Sperry's work on split brains, Nobel Prize 1981.
textes.Le détecteur de mensonges repère les men: The lie detector reliably catches liars.
textes.Il mesure le stress, pas le mensonge. Un: It measures stress, not lying. An anxious innocent person fails, a calm liar passes.
textes.Inventé en 1921 par John Larson ; l'un d: Invented in 1921 by John Larson; one of its promoters, William Marston, would go on to create Wonder Woman and her lasso of truth.
textes.Des images subliminales « Buvez Coca-Col: Subliminal “Drink Coca-Cola” images shown in a movie theater made sales jump.
textes.Personne n'a pu la reproduire, et le dir: No one could reproduce it, and the theater manager said no test had taken place. In 1962, James Vicary admitted it was a publicity stunt, with too little data to conclude anything.
textes.Vicary annonce ses résultats en 1957 pou: Vicary announced his results in 1957 to launch his company.
textes.Un cheval, Hans le Malin, semblait savoi: A horse, Clever Hans, seemed to know how to count, but was actually reading his audience's involuntary gestures.
textes.Le psychologue Oskar Pfungst montre en 1: The psychologist Oskar Pfungst showed in 1907 that he got it wrong as soon as the questioner did not know the answer.
textes.On appelle depuis « effet Hans le Malin: The experimenter's involuntary influence has been called the “Clever Hans effect” ever since.
textes.Dans une expérience célèbre, la majorité: In a famous experiment, most participants agreed to deliver apparently dangerous electric shocks on command.
textes.Dans l'expérience de Milgram, 65 % vont: In Milgram's experiment, 65% went all the way to 450 volts. There were no shocks: the “learner” was an actor in on it.
textes.Milgram cherchait à comprendre l'obéissa: Milgram was trying to understand obedience after the Eichmann trial.
textes.Des volontaires occupés à compter des pa: Volunteers busy counting basketball passes did not see a gorilla walk across the scene.
textes.Environ la moitié ne voit pas l'étudiant: About half do not see the student dressed as a gorilla. This is inattentional blindness.
textes.L'expérience de Simons et Chabris est de: Simons and Chabris's experiment has become a classic of the psychology of attention.
textes.Les caractères acquis au cours de la vie: Traits acquired during life are passed on to offspring: the giraffe lengthened its neck by stretching it.
textes.Ce sont les gènes qui se transmettent. L: It is genes that are passed on. Giraffes with slightly longer necks survived better and had more young.
textes.L'idée remonte à Lamarck. En URSS, Lysse: The idea goes back to Lamarck. In the USSR, Lysenko revived a version of it with the backing of the state and persecuted geneticists.
textes.Nous partageons avec lui un ancêtre comm: We share with them a common ancestor who lived several million years ago, between 5 and 13 depending on the estimates. The chimpanzee has evolved just as long as we have.
textes.Une caricature de Darwin, dessiné avec u: A caricature of Darwin, drawn with a monkey's body as early as 1871 in the newspaper The Hornet.
textes.Notre corps contient dix fois plus de ce: Our body contains ten times more bacterial cells than human cells.
textes.Une estimation récente donne à peu près: A recent estimate gives roughly as many of each, about 38 trillion bacteria for 30 trillion human cells.
textes.Le chiffre de dix pour un vient d'un cal: The ten-to-one figure comes from a quick 1972 calculation, copied for forty years.
textes.L'évolution mène vers des espèces de plu: Evolution leads toward more and more perfect species.
textes.La sélection naturelle n'a pas de but :: Natural selection has no goal: it favors what works in a given environment. Bacteria, which appeared more than 3 billion years ago, are doing very well.
textes.L'image populaire d'une échelle qui mont: The popular image of a ladder climbing up to humans, which Darwin avoided.
textes.Des poissons rouges ont appris à pousser: Goldfish have learned to push a lever to get food, and to do so at a precise time. Other experiments show memories lasting months.
textes.Une phrase répétée par les vendeurs d'aq: A phrase repeated by aquarium sellers, never measured.
textes.Ses promesses ne se sont jamais réalisée: His promises never came true: the mass introduction of vernalization was a failure. Lysenko only lost his institute in 1965, after Khrushchev's fall.
textes.Des résultats annoncés dans la presse du: Results announced in the party press, without controlled trials.
textes.Les autruches enfouissent leur tête dans: Ostriches bury their heads in the sand when they are afraid.
textes.Elles s'aplatissent au sol ou s'enfuient: They flatten themselves on the ground or run off at 70 km/h. They also lower their heads toward their nest, a simple hole in the ground, to turn their eggs.
textes.L'idée est déjà chez Pline l'Ancien, qui: The idea is already in Pliny the Elder, who thinks the bird believes itself hidden once it has stuck its neck into a bush.
textes.Le généticien Nikolaï Vavilov, opposant: The geneticist Nikolai Vavilov, Lysenko's opponent, died in prison.
textes.Arrêté en 1940, il meurt en 1943 dans la: Arrested in 1940, he died in 1943 in Saratov prison, worn out by detention; some authors speak of starvation. He had built up one of the largest seed collections in the world, which his colleagues protected during the siege of Leningrad.
textes.Son histoire n'a été racontée librement: His story was only told freely after Lysenko's fall.
textes.Des tardigrades ont survécu à une exposi: Tardigrades have survived direct exposure to the vacuum of space.
textes.En 2007, sur la mission FOTON-M3, des ta: In 2007, on the FOTON-M3 mission, dehydrated tardigrades spent ten days in space. The vacuum alone did almost nothing to them; some even survived part of the solar UV, then laid eggs.
textes.Ces animaux, le plus souvent plus petits: These animals, usually smaller than half a millimeter, withstand extreme conditions by drying out.
textes.Gregor Mendel a publié ses lois de l'hér: Gregor Mendel published his laws of heredity in 1866, but they were ignored for 34 years.
textes.Elles sont redécouvertes en 1900 par tro: They were rediscovered in 1900 by three botanists, de Vries, Correns and Tschermak.
textes.Mendel était moine, publiait dans une re: Mendel was a monk, published in a local journal, and became abbot before anyone read him.
textes.Les traînées blanches des avions sont de: The white trails behind planes are chemicals sprayed in secret.
textes.Ce sont des traînées de condensation : l: They are condensation trails: the water vapor from the engines freezes in the cold air. Of 77 experts surveyed, 76 found no trace of a secret program.
textes.La théorie des « chemtrails » se répand: The “chemtrails” theory spread in the late 1990s, drawing on a 1996 US Air Force forecasting exercise about weather control.
textes.Les missions Apollo sur la Lune ont été: The Apollo missions to the Moon were filmed in a studio.
textes.Des réflecteurs laissés par Apollo 11, 1: Reflectors left by Apollo 11, 14 and 15 send back laser shots fired from Earth, and the LRO probe has photographed the landing sites.
textes.Le livre de Bill Kaysing, We Never Went: Bill Kaysing's self-published book, We Never Went to the Moon, from 1976.
textes.Une étude sur plus de 650 000 enfants da: A study of more than 650,000 Danish children found no link. The article that claimed it was fraudulent.
textes.L'article d'Andrew Wakefield dans The La: Andrew Wakefield's 1998 article in The Lancet, retracted in 2010; Wakefield was struck off the medical register.
textes.Les pyramides d'Égypte sont trop parfait: The pyramids of Egypt are too perfect to have been built by humans of that era.
textes.On a retrouvé les villages des ouvriers: The workers' villages have been found at Giza, their tombs, and the diary of the inspector Merer describing the transport of the blocks.
textes.Popularisée en 1968 par Erich von Dänike: Popularized in 1968 by Erich von Däniken in Chariots of the Gods?
A virus does not travel by radio waves. The epidemic hit countries that had no 5G.
textes.Une rumeur de début 2020 ; au Royaume-Un: A rumor from early 2020; in the United Kingdom, antennas were set on fire.
textes.On a photographié un visage sculpté sur: A face carved on Mars has been photographed.
textes.La sonde Viking 1 a photographié en 1976: The Viking 1 probe photographed a hill in 1976 that looks like a face under a certain light. High-resolution photos from Mars Global Surveyor show a plain hill.
textes.C'est de la paréidolie, notre tendance à: It is pareidolia, our tendency to see faces everywhere.
textes.L'émission radio La Guerre des mondes d': Orson Welles's radio broadcast The War of the Worlds set off a mass panic in the United States in 1938.
textes.Très peu de gens l'écoutaient, et les té: Very few people were listening, and accounts of panic are rare. Newspapers, facing competition from radio, blew up the story.
textes.Une fausse nouvelle sur une fausse nouve: A false news story about a false news story, born in the next day's papers.
textes.Des médecins américains ont laissé des h: American doctors left men with syphilis untreated for 40 years, to observe the disease.
textes.L'étude de Tuskegee dure de 1932 à 1972,: The Tuskegee study lasted from 1932 to 1972, even after penicillin arrived. It was revealed in 1972 by the journalist Jean Heller, tipped off by the whistleblower Peter Buxtun.
textes.Un vrai complot, établi par des document: A real conspiracy, established by documents and investigations, which changed the rules of medical ethics.
textes.La CIA a fait prendre du LSD à des perso: The CIA gave people LSD without their consent.
textes.Le programme MKUltra, de 1953 à 1972, es: The MKUltra program, from 1953 to 1972, was revealed in 1975 by commissions of inquiry, then laid out before the Senate in 1977. Most of the records had been destroyed in 1973, but not all.
textes.Les vrais complots finissent souvent par: Real conspiracies often end up leaving documents behind.
textes.En 1962, l'état-major américain a propos: In 1962, the US Joint Chiefs of Staff proposed staging attacks to justify a war against Cuba.
textes.C'est l'opération Northwoods. Le gouvern: This is Operation Northwoods. The Kennedy administration rejected it. The document was declassified in 1997.
textes.Une proposition réelle, connue grâce aux: A real proposal, known thanks to public archives, and never carried out.
textes.L'homéopathie est plus efficace qu'un pl: Homeopathy is more effective than a placebo.
textes.L'analyse de 176 études par l'agence de: The Australian health agency's review of 176 studies found no condition for which it does better than a placebo. It has not been reimbursed in France since 2021.
textes.La grippe est due à un virus, les antibi: The flu is caused by a virus; antibiotics only act on bacteria. Taking them for nothing encourages resistance.
textes.Une confusion si répandue qu'elle a eu s: A confusion so widespread that it got its own French campaign: “Antibiotics are not automatic.”
textes.Le sang de nos veines est bleu tant qu'i: The blood in our veins is blue until it touches the air.
textes.Il est rouge sombre. Les veines paraisse: It is dark red. Veins look blue because the skin sends back blue light better than red.
textes.Les schémas qui colorient veines et artè: Diagrams that color veins and arteries blue and red.
textes.Se baigner juste après un repas expose à: Swimming right after a meal brings on cramps that make you drown.
textes.Une revue de la Croix-Rouge américaine n: A review by the American Red Cross found nothing linking a meal before swimming to a risk of drowning.
textes.Un conseil de prudence répété depuis des: A word of caution repeated for generations.
textes.La vitamine C à haute dose protège du rh: High-dose vitamin C protects against colds.
textes.Chez la plupart des gens, elle ne réduit: In most people, it does not reduce the number of colds, and only shortens them a little.
textes.Le double prix Nobel Linus Pauling en fa: The double Nobel laureate Linus Pauling promoted it in a 1970 book, Vitamin C and the Common Cold.
textes.Les cheveux et les ongles continuent de: Hair and nails keep growing after death.
textes.La peau se déshydrate et se rétracte, ce: The skin dries out and shrinks back, which makes them look longer. Growth requires living cells.
textes.Il faut boire au moins huit verres d'eau: You must drink at least eight glasses of water a day on top of what you eat.
textes.Aucune étude ne le justifie. Une bonne p: No study justifies it. A good share of our water comes from food and other drinks.
textes.Une recommandation américaine de 1945 pr: A 1945 American recommendation specified that most of this water was found in food. That sentence was forgotten.
textes.George Washington est mort après qu'on l: George Washington died after about 40% of his blood was drawn to treat him.
textes.En décembre 1799, ses médecins lui retir: In December 1799, his doctors drew about 2.4 liters of blood in twelve hours for a severe throat inflammation.
textes.La saignée était un traitement courant d: Bloodletting had been a common treatment since antiquity.
textes.Semmelweis a fait chuter la mortalité d': Semmelweis brought down a maternity ward's death rate by enforcing hand washing, and his colleagues rejected him.
textes.À Vienne en 1847, la mortalité de sa cli: In Vienna in 1847, his clinic's death rate fell from about 10% to 1 or 2%. But he could not explain it, and his colleagues took offense at being accused.
textes.Pasteur et Lister lui donneront raison v: Pasteur and Lister would prove him right twenty years later.
textes.Un placebo peut soulager même quand le p: A placebo can bring relief even when the patient knows it is a placebo.
textes.Dans un essai sur le syndrome de l'intes: In a trial on irritable bowel syndrome, patients who had been told still saw their symptoms decrease.
textes.L'effet placebo tient aussi au rituel du: The placebo effect also comes from the ritual of care.
textes.Les lemmings se jettent en masse du haut: Lemmings throw themselves off cliffs en masse.
textes.Leurs populations explosent puis s'effon: Their populations boom and then crash about every four years, and they then migrate in great numbers. They do not commit suicide.
textes.Le documentaire Disney White Wilderness: The Disney documentary White Wilderness (1958), whose crew threw the same lemmings off a cliff several times.
textes.Les bovins distinguent mal le rouge. C'e: Cattle see red poorly. It is the movement of the cape that triggers the charge: waved about, a blue cape has the same effect.
textes.La muleta des corridas est rouge, surtou: The muleta used in bullfights is red, mainly to hide the blood.
textes.Toutes voient, et les grandes roussettes: All bats can see, and large fruit bats even have very good eyesight. Many also find their way by echolocation.
textes.À la fin du XVIIIe siècle, Spallanzani c: In the late 18th century, Spallanzani found that bats with blinded eyes still avoided obstacles. People concluded they did not need their eyes.
textes.Un ver de terre coupé en deux donne deux: An earthworm cut in two makes two worms.
textes.Selon l'espèce et l'endroit de la coupur: Depending on the species and where the cut is, a single piece sometimes survives and regrows what it is missing, usually the one that keeps the band, the clitellum.
textes.Une confusion avec les planaires, des ve: A confusion with planarians, flatworms that really do regrow a whole individual from a piece.
textes.Les dromadaires stockent de l'eau dans l: Camels store water in their hump.
textes.La bosse est une réserve de graisse. Leu: The hump is a fat reserve. Their endurance comes from very thrifty kidneys and red blood cells that can swell when they drink a lot at once.
textes.Une explication intuitive : une bosse po: An intuitive explanation: a hump for the crossing.
textes.Le porc-épic projette ses piquants sur s: The porcupine shoots its quills at its enemies.
textes.Il ne peut pas les lancer. Les piquants: It cannot throw them. The quills come loose on contact and stay stuck in the attacker.
textes.Pline l'Ancien l'affirme dans son Histoi: Pliny the Elder claims it in his Natural History, and the legend has come down through the centuries.
textes.Les hirondelles passent l'hiver endormie: Swallows spend the winter asleep at the bottom of ponds.
textes.Elles migrent jusqu'en Afrique, ce qu'on: They migrate as far as Africa, which was accepted by the late 18th century; bird ringing, begun in 1899, confirmed it.
textes.Aristote parle d'hirondelles qui se cach: Aristotle speaks of swallows that hide in winter. In 1555, Archbishop Olaus Magnus tells of fishermen hauling them up in netfuls from the bottom of lakes.
textes.Les deux tiers des neurones d'une pieuvr: Two thirds of an octopus's neurons are in its arms.
textes.Sur environ 500 millions de neurones, la: Of about 500 million neurons, most are in the arms, which can taste, grasp and react without waiting for the brain.
textes.Des comptages de neurones et des expérie: Neuron counts and experiments on isolated arms.
textes.Les corneilles reconnaissent un visage h: Crows recognize a human face and remember it for years.
textes.À Seattle, des chercheurs masqués ont ca: In Seattle, masked researchers captured a few crows. Years later, the birds still screamed at that mask, including those that had never been captured.
textes.Une expérience menée avec des masques de: An experiment run with rubber masks, to separate the face from the person.
textes.En 1822, une cigogne est arrivée en Alle: In 1822, a stork arrived in Germany with an African spear stuck through its neck.
textes.Cette « cigogne à flèche » a prouvé que: This “arrow stork” proved that storks wintered in Africa, at a time when the great migrations were still doubted.
textes.L'oiseau naturalisé est toujours exposé: The stuffed bird is still on display at the University of Rostock.
textes.On repère un menteur à son regard, qui p: You can spot a liar by their gaze, which goes up and to the right.
textes.Des chercheurs ont filmé des personnes q: Researchers filmed people who were lying or telling the truth: the direction of their gaze did not tell them apart.
textes.Le polygraphe mesure le stress : pouls,: The polygraph measures stress: pulse, breathing, sweat. An anxious innocent person can fail, a calm liar can pass.
textes.Inventé en 1921 par John Larson, popular: Invented in 1921 by John Larson, popularized by William Marston, who also created Wonder Woman and her lasso of truth.
textes.La mémoire enregistre les événements com: Memory records events like a video that can be replayed faithfully.
textes.Chaque souvenir se reconstruit quand on: Every memory is rebuilt when it is recalled. You can even make people believe they got lost in a shopping mall as children.
textes.La métaphore de l'enregistrement, et l'a: The recording metaphor, and the “recovered memories” affair of the 1990s.
textes.Une soirée trop arrosée détruit des mill: One heavy night of drinking destroys thousands of neurons.
textes.L'alcool perturbe les neurones et, à lon: Alcohol disrupts neurons and, in the long term and at high doses, damages their connections. But no loss of cortical neurons is found in heavy drinkers.
textes.Une formule de prévention qui a pris le: A prevention slogan that took a shortcut.
textes.Il faut ajouter au moins l'équilibre, la: You must add at least balance, body position, temperature and pain. Physiologists count about ten, or even more.
Aristotle's list, in On the Soul.
textes.La langue a des zones séparées pour le s: The tongue has separate areas for sweet, salty, sour and bitter.
textes.Toutes les parties de la langue qui port: Every part of the tongue that has taste buds perceives every taste.
textes.Une thèse allemande de 1901, dont les co: A 1901 German thesis whose curves, redrawn in 1942 by the psychologist Edwin Boring, were misread and then copied into textbooks.
textes.Le cerveau d'Einstein était plus gros qu: Einstein's brain was bigger than average.
textes.Il pesait environ 1 230 grammes, dans le: It weighed about 1,230 grams, at the low end of the normal range. Some regions had an unusual shape, which does not prove much.
textes.On imagine le génie proportionnel à la t: People imagine genius as proportional to size, like the phrenologists.
textes.Le cerveau consomme environ 20 % de l'én: The brain uses about 20% of the body's energy at rest, for 2% of its mass.
textes.Il ne s'éteint jamais : même au repos, i: It never switches off: even at rest, it maintains its neurons and their exchanges.
textes.Des mesures de consommation d'oxygène et: Measurements of oxygen and glucose consumption by imaging.
textes.En 1848, Phineas Gage a survécu à une ba: In 1848, Phineas Gage survived an iron bar that went through his skull.
textes.Il a vécu encore douze ans. Son caractèr: He lived another twelve years. His personality is said to have changed, which made him a textbook case on the role of the frontal lobe.
textes.Le récit de son médecin, John Harlow, et: The account of his doctor, John Harlow, and the skull kept at Harvard.
textes.On peut avoir mal dans un bras qu'on n'a: You can feel pain in an arm you no longer have.
textes.C'est la douleur du membre fantôme. Un s: This is phantom limb pain. A simple mirror, which shows the remaining arm in place of the other one, relieves some patients.
textes.Les premiers humains ont côtoyé les dino: The first humans lived alongside dinosaurs.
textes.Les derniers dinosaures non aviens dispa: The last non-avian dinosaurs disappeared 66 million years ago; Homo sapiens is about 300,000 years old.
textes.Les coquillages fossiles trouvés en mont: Fossil shells found in the mountains prove a universal flood.
textes.La tectonique des plaques soulève d'anci: Plate tectonics lifts up ancient seabeds: the summit of Everest is made of marine limestone.
textes.Une explication courante jusqu'au XVIIIe: A common explanation until the 18th century. Leonardo da Vinci already disputed it: for him, mountains were ancient seabeds raised little by little.
textes.Les mutations surviennent au hasard, mai: Mutations occur at random, but the natural selection that sorts them does not: it keeps what works.
textes.Un résumé trompeur du darwinisme, souven: A misleading summary of Darwinism, often used to reject it.
textes.Les dinosaures n'ont aucun lien avec les: Dinosaurs have no connection with birds.
textes.Les oiseaux sont des dinosaures théropod: Birds are theropod dinosaurs, and many dinosaurs had feathers.
textes.Les reconstitutions du XIXe siècle, en g: The 19th-century reconstructions as big four-legged lizards, like the ones at the Crystal Palace in London in 1854.
textes.Les Néandertaliens étaient des brutes sa: Neanderthals were cultureless brutes, unrelated to us.
textes.Ils enterraient leurs morts et fabriquai: They buried their dead and made ornaments. Humans of non-African descent carry about 2% Neanderthal DNA.
textes.La reconstitution voûtée de Marcellin Bo: Marcellin Boule's stooped reconstruction, published from 1911 to 1913, based on the skeleton of an old man with osteoarthritis.
textes.Les derniers mammouths avaient disparu b: The last mammoths had disappeared long before the pyramids of Egypt were built.
textes.Une petite population a vécu sur l'île W: A small population lived on Wrangel Island, in Siberia, until about 4,000 years ago, a few centuries after the Great Pyramid of Giza.

textes.Pour additionner des fractions, on les m: To add fractions, put them over a common denominator: 3/4 + 1/8 = 6/8 + 1/8 = 7/8. You never add the denominators.
textes.Diviser par une fraction, c'est multipli: Dividing by a fraction means multiplying by its reciprocal: 2 ÷ 1/2 = 4.
textes.Un nombre premier a exactement deux divi: A prime number has exactly two divisors, 1 and itself. So 1 is not prime; 2 is the only even prime.
textes.6 ÷ 2 × 3 vaut 9, pas 1 : à priorité éga: 6 ÷ 2 × 3 equals 9, not 1: with equal priority, the convention is to work from left to right.

textes.Règle de trois, échelles, hausses et bai: Rule of three, scales, percentage increases and decreases.
textes.La règle de trois marche quand deux gran: The rule of three works when two quantities are proportional: if 3 kg cost €12, 5 kg cost 5 × 12 / 3 = €20.
textes.Une hausse de t % multiplie par (1 + t/1: An increase of t% multiplies by (1 + t/100), a decrease by (1 − t/100). Successive changes chain by multiplying the coefficients.
textes.+50 % puis −50 % ne ramène pas au départ: +50% then −50% does not bring you back to the start: 1.5 × 0.5 = 0.75, a 25% drop.
textes.Point de pourcentage et pourcentage diff: Percentage points and percent differ: going from 10% to 12% is +2 points, but +20%.
textes.Une baisse de 20 % ne se rattrape pas pa: A 20% drop is not made up by a 20% rise: you need +25%.
textes.Hausse de 50 % puis baisse de 50 % : on: A 50% rise then a 50% drop: you end up at 75
textes.Le hasard, l'indépendance, les paradoxes: Chance, independence, the paradoxes that fool intuition.
textes.Probabilité = cas favorables ÷ cas possi: Probability = favorable cases ÷ possible cases, provided the cases are equally likely.
textes.Deux événements indépendants : on multip: Two independent events: multiply their probabilities. Two heads in a row: 1/2 × 1/2 = 1/4.
textes.Le hasard n'a pas de mémoire : après dix: Chance has no memory: after ten heads, the eleventh toss still has a one in two chance (the gambler's fallacy).
textes.Monty Hall : changer de porte fait gagne: Monty Hall: switching doors wins 2 times out of 3, because the host knows where the car is and never opens that door.
textes.Avec deux dés, 7 est la somme la plus pr: With two dice, 7 is the most likely sum (6 outcomes out of 36), not 12 (1 out of 36).
textes.Tableau des 36 résultats possibles avec: Table of the 36 possible results with two dice

textes.« Si A alors B » est faux dans un seul c: “If A then B” is false in only one case: A true and B false.
textes.La contraposée « si non B alors non A »: The contrapositive “if not B then not A” is equivalent. The converse “if B then A” is not.
textes.Nier « tous les cygnes sont blancs », c': Negating “all swans are white” means saying “at least one swan is not white”, not “no swan is white”.
textes.Raisonnement par l'absurde : on suppose: Proof by contradiction: assume the opposite of what you want to prove and reach a contradiction.
textes.Affirmer le conséquent : « s'il pleut, l: Affirming the consequent: “if it rains, the ground is wet; the ground is wet, so it's raining” is invalid.

textes.Résoudre une équation : faire la même op: Solving an equation: do the same operation on both sides until the unknown is isolated.
textes.Identités remarquables : (a + b)² = a² +: Special products: (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b², (a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b², (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b².

textes.Diviser les deux côtés par x fait perdre: Dividing both sides by x loses the solution x = 0: factor instead.
textes.Moyenne, médiane, écart type, corrélatio: Mean, median, standard deviation, correlation and samples.
textes.La moyenne est sensible aux valeurs extr: The mean is sensitive to extreme values; the median splits the population into two halves and resists them.
textes.Quand Bill Gates entre dans un bar, la m: When Bill Gates walks into a bar, the mean fortune explodes; the median barely moves.
textes.L'écart type mesure la dispersion autour: The standard deviation measures the spread around the mean.
textes.Corrélation n'est pas causalité : glaces: Correlation is not causation: ice cream and drownings rise together in summer, because of the heat.
textes.Un salaire moyen supérieur au salaire mé: An average salary above the median salary doesn't mean most people earn more than the average: it's the opposite.
textes.Cinq valeurs : médiane 2, moyenne 4 tiré: Five values: median 2, mean 4 pulled up by the value 12
textes.Angles, aires, volumes, Pythagore, sinus: Angles, areas, volumes, Pythagoras, sine and cosine.
textes.Pythagore : dans un triangle rectangle,: Pythagoras: in a right triangle, the square of the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides (3, 4, 5).
textes.Aire du disque π r², périmètre 2 π r ; v: Area of a disk π r², circumference 2 π r; volume of a sphere 4/3 π r³.
textes.Doubler les longueurs multiplie les aire: Doubling lengths multiplies areas by 4 and volumes by 8.
textes.Dans un triangle rectangle : sinus = opp: In a right triangle: sine = opposite / hypotenuse, cosine = adjacent / hypotenuse, tangent = opposite / adjacent.
textes.La somme des angles d'un triangle vaut 1: The angles of a triangle add up to 180°, but only on a plane: on a sphere, they add up to more than 180°.
textes.Agrandir une figure : longueurs, aires e: Enlarging a figure: lengths, areas and volumes
textes.Suites, séries, limites et les paradoxes: Sequences, series, limits and the paradoxes of infinity.
textes.Une suite géométrique de raison inférieu: A geometric sequence with ratio less than 1 in absolute value tends to 0; its sum can be finite: 1/2 + 1/4 + 1/8 + … = 1.
textes.0,999… = 1 exactement : c'est la même so: 0.999… = 1 exactly: it's the same infinite sum written another way.
textes.La série harmonique 1 + 1/2 + 1/3 + … di: The harmonic series 1 + 1/2 + 1/3 + … diverges, even though its terms tend to 0.
textes.Cantor : il y a autant d'entiers pairs q: Cantor: there are as many even integers as integers, but strictly more real numbers than integers.
textes.Que les termes tendent vers 0 ne suffit: Terms tending to 0 is not enough for an infinite sum to be finite.
textes.Les sommes 1/2 + 1/4 + … s'approchent de: The sums 1/2 + 1/4 + … approach 1 without exceeding it
textes.Cette tablette d'argile, achetée par Geo: This clay tablet, bought by George Plimpton around 1922, holds a table of numbers satisfying a² + b² = c², a millennium before Pythagoras.
textes.François Viète publie un calcul où les l: François Viète publishes a calculus in which letters replace numbers.
textes.Son Introduction à l'art analytique note: His Introduction to the Analytic Art writes unknowns as vowels and known quantities as consonants. Viète, an adviser to Henri IV, also cracked Spanish secret codes: Philip II accused him of sorcery before the pope.
textes.Publication posthume de l'essai de Thoma: Posthumous publication of Thomas Bayes's essay.
textes.Le pasteur Thomas Bayes n'a jamais publi: The minister Thomas Bayes never published his theorem: his friend Richard Price found it among his papers and had it published two years after his death.
textes.Lobatchevski publie une géométrie où les: Lobachevsky publishes a geometry in which parallel lines behave differently.
textes.Bolyai fait la même découverte de son cô: Bolyai makes the same discovery on his own. Gauss had thought of it without publishing, for fear of “the clamor of the Boeotians”, as he wrote.
textes.George Boole, autodidacte, réduit le rai: George Boole, self-taught, reduces reasoning to calculations on 0 and 1. Claude Shannon would use it in 1937 to design electrical circuits.
textes.Florence Nightingale montre en graphique: Florence Nightingale shows in charts that soldiers die mostly of preventable diseases.
textes.Ses diagrammes polaires, présentés au go: Her polar area diagrams, presented to the British government, helped reform hygiene in military hospitals. She was the first woman elected to the Royal Statistical Society, in 1858.
textes.Georg Cantor montre qu'on ne peut pas nu: Georg Cantor shows that the real numbers cannot all be numbered.
textes.Son travail choque une partie des mathém: His work shocked some mathematicians, including Kronecker. Hilbert would later say: “No one shall expel us from the paradise that Cantor has created for us.”
textes.Francis Galton retrouve la corrélation e: Francis Galton rediscovers correlation by comparing heights and forearm lengths.
textes.Cousin de Darwin, Galton invente aussi l: A cousin of Darwin, Galton also invented the questionnaire, fingerprints in criminology and, unfortunately, the word “eugenics”.
textes.Un rouleau de près de cinq mètres, copié: A scroll nearly five meters long, copied by the scribe Ahmes from an older text. It gathers eighty-seven solved problems, like a workbook: sharing loaves among ten men, computing the volume of a granary, the slope of a pyramid. The Egyptians wrote their fractions as sums of fractions with numerator one, and the papyrus provides tables to handle them. For the area of a disk, it removes one ninth from the diameter and squares the rest, which amounts to taking pi as about 3.16. No proofs: recipes, checked on examples.
textes.C'est l'un des plus anciens manuels de m: It is one of the oldest mathematics textbooks to have come down to us.
textes.Ahmès l'a intitulé, sans fausse modestie: Ahmes titled it, with no false modesty, “correct method of reckoning, for grasping the meaning of things and knowing everything”. The Scotsman Rhind bought it in Luxor in 1858.
textes.Connaître tous les secrets, en quatre-vi: Knowing all secrets, in eighty-four exercises. I give you fewer, and you already find it a lot.
textes.anglais, trad. de l'égyptien par A. B. C: English, translated from Egyptian by A. B. Chace
textes.Treize livres pour bâtir toute la géomét: Thirteen books to build all of geometry from almost nothing: a few definitions (a point, a line), five postulates accepted without proof, and common notions such as “the whole is greater than the part”. From there, Euclid proves hundreds of propositions step by step: the Pythagorean theorem, the construction of regular polygons, the infinitude of prime numbers. Each result rests on the previous ones, like the floors of a building. The fifth postulate, the one about parallels, intrigued mathematicians for two thousand years; by replacing it, they invented non-Euclidean geometries in the 19th century.
textes.Il a fixé pour des siècles ce que veut d: It set for centuries what it means to “prove”.
textes.Abraham Lincoln raconte avoir étudié, et: Abraham Lincoln said he studied, and nearly mastered, the first six books after his term in Congress.
textes.Treize livres, et pas une phrase de trop: Thirteen books, and not one sentence too many. The AI sees in it a model your answers could follow.
A point is that which has no part.
