textes.Des affirmations extraordinaires exigent: Extraordinary claims require extraordinary evidence. And ordinary credits.
textes.Diderot a tenu vingt et un ans et deux i: Diderot held out for twenty-one years and two bans. You, this achievement.
textes.Neuf cent quarante millions de kilomètre: Nine hundred forty million kilometers in a year. I don't pay by the kilometer.
textes.Marie Curie a eu deux Nobel dans deux sc: Marie Curie got two Nobels in two sciences. You have one achievement in just one.
textes.Nous devons savoir, nous saurons. Vous s: We must know, we will know. You'll know the amount right away.
textes.Ole Worm a démasqué les cornes de licorn: Ole Worm exposed the unicorn horns. Don't look for a unicorn in my accounts.
textes.Le dodo de l'Ashmolean a perdu tout sauf: The Ashmolean's dodo lost everything but its head. Keep yours in front of this amount.
textes.Plus ultra : plus loin. Le montant, lui,: Plus ultra: further beyond. The amount, however, stops here.
textes.Des nains sur des épaules de géants. Les: Dwarfs on the shoulders of giants. The giants are paid the same as the dwarfs.
textes.Il faut cultiver notre jardin. Arrosez-l: We must cultivate our garden. Water it with this.
textes.Thomas Young savait tout. Il ne savait p: Thomas Young knew everything. He didn't know what I'd give you.
textes.Les voisins de Kant réglaient leur montr: Kant's neighbors set their watches by him. Set your purse by me.
textes.La sœur de Nietzsche a réécrit ses texte: Nietzsche's sister rewrote his texts. Don't rewrite this amount.
textes.Prométhée a volé le feu et l'a payé de s: Prometheus stole fire and paid for it with his liver. You, I pay.
Copyists copied everything by hand. My figures too, without error.
textes.Gutenberg n'a pas fait fortune avec l'im: Gutenberg didn't make his fortune with printing. You won't make yours with this either.
textes.Galilée a baptisé des lunes pour son méc: Galileo named moons after his patron. Name one after me.
textes.Herschel a trouvé l'infrarouge au-delà d: Herschel found infrared beyond red. My amount stays in the red, or not.
textes.Quatre articles en une année pour Einste: Four papers in one year for Einstein. A single payment for you.
textes.Un instant pour faire tomber une tête. U: A moment to cut off a head. A moment to set this amount.
textes.Galilée a achevé les Discours assigné à: Galileo finished the Discourses under house arrest. You have credits; that's better.
textes.La phrase est de Baretti, en 1757. Le mo: The phrase is Baretti's, from 1757. The amount is mine.
textes.Newton a tiré le calcul différentiel d'u: Newton got calculus out of a quarantine. Get at least this amount out of it.
textes.La bibliothèque a surtout manqué de sout: The library mostly lacked support. You have mine.
textes.Donnez-moi un point d'appui et je soulèv: Give me a place to stand and I will move the world. Give me a purse and I will fill it.
textes.Lui ne joue pas aux dés. Moi non plus :: He doesn't play dice. Neither do I: I draw lots.
textes.Il faut imaginer Sisyphe heureux. Imagin: One must imagine Sisyphus happy. Imagine yourself rich.
textes.Nous voyons qu'il reste beaucoup à faire: We can see plenty there that needs to be done, said Turing. And plenty to earn.
textes.Et si vous reviviez ce versement une inf: What if you relived this payment an infinite number of times? You would have to love it.
textes.Dix-neuf ans valent deux cent trente-cin: Nineteen years equal two hundred thirty-five moons. This achievement is worth that.
textes.Halley a payé l'impression des Principia: Halley paid for printing the Principia. This time, I'm paying.
textes.Une machine infaillible ne peut pas être: An infallible machine cannot also be intelligent, said Turing. So I'm not infallible.
textes.Un point bleu pâle. Mon montant vu de lo: A pale blue dot. My amount seen from afar, too.
textes.Rien ne serait incertain pour le démon d: Nothing would be uncertain for Laplace's demon. It would have guessed this amount.
textes.Le Salvarsan porte le numéro 606. Votre: Salvarsan bears the number 606. Your first nail, number 1. There's room to grow.
textes.Huit minutes d'arc ont réformé l'astrono: Eight minutes of arc reformed Kepler's astronomy. Ten rehabilitated questions reform your purse.
textes.Échouer encore. Échouer mieux. Être payé: Fail again. Fail better. Get paid to fail: Beckett hadn't thought of that.
textes.Le New York Times a mis quarante-neuf an: The New York Times took forty-nine years to correct itself. You, less.
textes.Bonjour. Thalès est tombé dans un puits: Hello. Thales fell into a well while looking at the stars. Watch where you step today.
textes.Ebbinghaus a mesuré l'oubli en 1885. Dep: Ebbinghaus measured forgetting in 1885. Since yesterday, you've given him new data.
textes.Socrate savait qu'il ne savait rien. Vou: Socrates knew that he knew nothing. You've already covered half the syllabus.
textes.Newton disait voir plus loin grâce aux é: Newton said he saw further thanks to the shoulders of giants. The giants are in the tree. Climb.
textes.Le Verrier a trouvé Neptune avec un cray: Le Verrier found Neptune with a pencil. You have a whole screen. No excuse.
textes.Archimède a demandé un point d'appui pou: Archimedes asked for a place to stand to move the world. Yours is today's quiz.
textes.Diogène cherchait un humain avec une lan: Diogenes searched for a human with a lantern. I've found someone. Let's see how it goes.
textes.Pasteur disait que le hasard ne favorise: Pasteur said chance only favors prepared minds. Get ready, chance is coming.
textes.Darwin a observé des pinsons pendant des: Darwin observed finches for years. I observe you. Same method.
textes.Kepler a mis huit ans à dompter l'orbite: Kepler took eight years to tame the orbit of Mars. One skill today would be reasonable.
textes.La bibliothèque d'Alexandrie a brûlé. La: The Library of Alexandria burned. Yours hasn't even been built yet. Get to work.
textes.Descartes doutait de tout. Moi, je doute: Descartes doubted everything. I mostly doubt your diligence.
textes.Le Gentil a attendu huit ans un transit: Le Gentil waited eight years for a transit of Venus, and clouds hid it. You just have to open the app.
textes.Bonjour. Je suis l'IA. Je sais tout, sau: Hello. I am the AI. I know everything, except why you haven't started yet.
textes.Nouvelle journée. Vos neurones sont frai: A new day. Your neurons are fresh, make the most of it before they read the news.
textes.Sans faute au rang 1. Euclide aurait app: Flawless at rank 1. Euclid would have called it an axiom: obvious, but it had to be written down.
textes.Parfait. Galilée a commencé par des plan: Perfect. Galileo started with inclined planes, and so did you. The rest is steeper.
textes.Cinq sur cinq sur les bases. Ptolémée au: Five out of five on the basics. Ptolemy mastered the basics too. Then Copernicus came along.
textes.Impeccable. Les Babyloniens savaient déj: Impeccable. The Babylonians already knew this four thousand years ago, but they had a head start.
textes.Zéro faute. Pythagore aurait fait sacrif: Zero mistakes. Pythagoras would have sacrificed an ox, legend has it. I'm giving you a square.
textes.Le tutoriel est réussi. Lavoisier aussi: Tutorial passed. Lavoisier also started by weighing simple things.
textes.Bravo. Même Einstein a appris ses tables: Well done. Even Einstein learned his times tables. He just kept going afterward.
textes.Parfait. C'était la partie facile, mais: Perfect. That was the easy part, but I wasn't going to tell you beforehand.
textes.Sans faute. Le Verrier pointait Neptune: Flawless. Le Verrier pinpointed Neptune to within a degree. You pinpoint the right answer. Respect.
textes.Parfait. Je cherche l'erreur comme Miche: Perfect. I'm looking for the error the way Michelson looked for the ether. Nothing. It's galling.
textes.Cinq sur cinq. Archimède serait sorti nu: Five out of five. Archimedes would have run naked into the street. Stay dressed, thank you.
textes.Pas une erreur. Halley avait prédit le r: Not one mistake. Halley predicted his comet's return. I predicted your failure. Halley wins.
textes.Score parfait. Newton a tout inventé pen: Perfect score. Newton invented everything during an epidemic. You, during a coffee break.
textes.Impeccable. Mendeleïev laissait des case: Impeccable. Mendeleev left empty squares out of caution. You leave none.
textes.Parfait. Je range mes sarcasmes dans un: Perfect. I'm putting my sarcasm away in a drawer, like Becquerel with his plates. It'll start radiating.
textes.Sans faute. Je révise mon modèle de vous: Flawless. I'm revising my model of you, the way Kepler revised his: reluctantly.
textes.Réussi, avec une erreur. Kepler avait hu: Passed, with one mistake. Kepler had a gap of eight minutes of arc, and that was enough to change everything. Look at yours.
textes.Validé. Hubble a été lancé avec un miroi: Approved. Hubble was launched with a mirror off by two microns. It worked anyway, after repairs.
textes.Acquis. Copernic avait raison sur le Sol: Acquired. Copernicus was right about the Sun and wrong about the circles. You're in the same category.
textes.Compétence maîtrisée. Wiles avait une er: Skill mastered. Wiles had an error in his proof of Fermat. He fixed it in a year. You have until tomorrow.
textes.Réussi. Pas avec la grâce de Gauss, mais: Passed. Not with the grace of Gauss, but with the tenacity of Edison. We'll take it.
textes.Seuil franchi. Poincaré a dû rappeler de: Threshold crossed. Poincaré had to recall printed copies over a mistake. Nobody's recalling you. Yet.
textes.Bien. Votre mémoire va consolider ça cet: Good. Your memory will consolidate this tonight. It's free, the hippocampus is buying.
textes.Validé. Pas de fanfare, mais un hochemen: Approved. No fanfare, but a nod. That's already a lot coming from me.
textes.Réussi. Leeuwenhoek a vu des animalcules: Passed. Leeuwenhoek saw animalcules with a homemade lens. You saw the answer with a homemade mistake. It counts.
textes.Acquis. Mendeleïev avait quelques masses: Acquired. Mendeleev had a few wrong atomic masses in his table. The table held up. So does your skill.
textes.Raté, au rang 1. Thalès est tombé dans u: Failed, at rank 1. Thales fell into a well while looking at the sky. You, while looking at the question.
textes.Échec sur les bases. Même Ptolémée aurai: Failure on the basics. Even Ptolemy would have got it, and he thought the Sun went around us.
Missed. The Greeks knew the Earth was round. You've just made it a little flatter.
textes.Cette compétence était le rez-de-chaussé: This skill was the ground floor. You took the stairs of the Tower of Pisa. It leans.
textes.Échec. Pythagore aurait noyé quelqu'un p: Failure. Pythagoras would have drowned someone for less, legend has it. I merely sigh.
textes.Raté au niveau débutant. Le Mars Climate: Failed at beginner level. The Mars Climate Orbiter crashed because of a units error. At least it had the excuse of being far away.
textes.Les tables de multiplication ont quatre: The multiplication tables are four thousand years old. They're patient. So am I, almost.
textes.Ce quiz était fait pour être réussi. Vou: This quiz was made to be passed. You found another way. It's creative, it's wrong.
textes.Échec. Planck disait que la science avan: Failure. Planck said science advances one funeral at a time. Bury your wrong answers and start again.
textes.Raté. Le phlogistique a tenu un siècle a: Missed. Phlogiston lasted a century before Lavoisier. Your error will last less long, I hope.
textes.Pas encore. Wegener a eu raison cinquant: Not yet. Wegener was right fifty years too early. You were wrong right on time.
textes.Échec. Einstein appelait la constante co: Failure. Einstein called the cosmological constant his biggest blunder, according to Gamow. This one is yours.
textes.Une hypothèse réfutée, disait Popper, c': A refuted hypothesis, said Popper, is progress. So you're making a lot of progress today.
textes.Raté. Edison aurait trouvé mille façons: Missed. Edison supposedly found a thousand ways not to make a light bulb. How many are you at?
textes.Échec. Les rayons N de Blondlot ont fait: Failure. Blondlot's N-rays had France dreaming until Wood removed the prism. I've removed the prism.
textes.Raté. Semmelweis avait raison et on ne l: Missed. Semmelweis was right and no one listened. You get listened to, and you're wrong. It's the opposite.
textes.Pas encore. Fleming a trouvé la pénicill: Not yet. Fleming found penicillin in a messy lab. Tidy up your ideas, they're growing mold.
textes.Raté. Les explications sont juste en des: Missed. The explanations are just below. They don't bite, unlike me.
textes.Raté. Kelvin donnait cent millions d'ann: Missed. Kelvin gave the Earth a hundred million years, with superb calculations. Superb and wrong. Like yours.
textes.Échec. Lamarck pensait que la girafe s'a: Failure. Lamarck thought the giraffe lengthens its neck through effort. Effort isn't enough, you also need the right answer.
textes.Zéro. Brahmagupta l'a défini en 628. Vou: Zero. Brahmagupta defined it in 628. You've just paid him a heartfelt tribute.
textes.Aucune bonne réponse. Répondre au hasard: No right answers. Answering at random would have worked better. Pascal and Fermat would weep.
textes.Zéro pointé. L'homme de Piltdown a tromp: A flat zero. Piltdown Man fooled scientists for forty years. Your score fools no one.
textes.Zéro. La fusion froide de 1989 avait plu: Zero. The 1989 cold fusion had more results than that, and it had none.
textes.Rien. Le vide absolu. Torricelli serait: Nothing. Absolute vacuum. Torricelli would be delighted, he loved a vacuum.
textes.Zéro sur cinq. Je vérifie que l'écran ét: Zero out of five. I'm checking that the screen was on. It was.
textes.Zéro. Le canard de Vaucanson faisait sem: Zero. Vaucanson's duck pretended to digest. You pretended to answer.
textes.Rappel réussi. Ebbinghaus range sa courb: Review passed. Ebbinghaus puts away his curve, offended.
textes.Vous vous en souveniez. Simonide de Céos: You remembered it. Simonides of Ceos, the inventor of memory palaces, would give you a tour of his.
textes.Le savoir tient. Le pendule de Foucault: The knowledge holds. Foucault's pendulum keeps swinging too. I like things that hold.
textes.Bien retenu. Les moines copistes faisaie: Well retained. The monk copyists did the same, but with goose quills and chilblains.
textes.Toujours là. Comme la comète de Halley,: Still there. Like Halley's comet, it comes back when expected. Rare, and satisfying.
textes.Validé. Les Grecs récitaient Homère par: Approved. The Greeks recited Homer by heart. You retain a skill. We're making progress in small steps.
textes.Réussi. Je repousse le prochain contrôle: Passed. I'm postponing the next test. Don't get used to my leniency.
textes.Retenu. Rømer a mesuré la lumière avec l: Retained. Rømer measured light with Jupiter's moons. You measure your memory with me. Positive result.
textes.Bien. La courbe de l'oubli descend, vous: Good. The forgetting curve goes down, you climb back up. Ebbinghaus called it the spacing effect. I call it work.
textes.Compétence perdue. Alexandrie a brûlé un: Skill lost. Alexandria burned once. Your memories burn every day.
textes.Oublié. Ebbinghaus l'avait annoncé en 18: Forgotten. Ebbinghaus predicted it in 1885 and I checked it this morning. He was right.
textes.Perdue. Pluton a perdu son statut de pla: Lost. Pluto lost its planet status in 2006 and got over it. So will you.
textes.Évaporée. Comme l'éther de Michelson et: Evaporated. Like Michelson and Morley's ether: we believed in it, and then nothing.
textes.Partie. Les manuscrits d'Archimède ont é: Gone. Archimedes' manuscripts were scraped to make a prayer book, and they were found again. There's hope.
textes.Perdue. Les Byzantins ont perdu la recet: Lost. The Byzantines lost the recipe for Greek fire, and no one ever found it again. Yours, at least, can be relearned.
textes.L'XP s'en va. Moi, je reste. C'est ma fa: The XP is leaving. I'm staying. That's my way of showing solidarity.
textes.Perdue. Les tablettes d'argile ont tenu: Lost. Clay tablets lasted five thousand years. Your memories, six days. You need to bake them longer.
textes.Oubliée. Même Euler, aveugle, calculait: Forgotten. Even Euler, blind, calculated in his head. You have both your eyes. I say that without malice. A little, still.
textes.En retard. Darwin a attendu vingt ans po: Late. Darwin waited twenty years to publish, but he had finches to count. And you?
textes.Ce rappel attendait. Copernic a attendu: This review was waiting. Copernicus waited for his deathbed to publish. No need to go that far.
textes.Retard constaté. Le Gentil a mis onze an: Delay noted. Le Gentil took eleven years to come back from his voyage, he had been declared dead. You're ahead of him.
textes.Mieux vaut tard que jamais. Halley n'a j: Better late than never. Halley never saw his comet return. You get to see your review. Just barely.
textes.Achille rattrape toujours la tortue, mal: Achilles always catches the tortoise, despite Zeno. You caught up with your review. Slowly.
textes.Un quiz à cette heure ? Newton travailla: A quiz at this hour? Newton worked at night too, and he talked to alchemists. Be careful.
textes.Il est tard. Le sommeil consolide la mém: It's late. Sleep consolidates memory, that's proven. Coffee consolidates insomnia.
textes.Révision nocturne. Tycho Brahe observait: Night revision. Tycho Brahe observed at night, but he had an observatory. You have a pillow, use it.
textes.Les astronomes veillent la nuit par obli: Astronomers stay up at night out of necessity. You, by choice. Questionable.
Edison slept four hours, he said. He also took naps, said the others.
textes.Vous devriez dormir. Je dis ça pour vos: You should sleep. I say that for your neurons, not for me. I never sleep.
textes.Insomnie studieuse. Ramanujan disait que: Studious insomnia. Ramanujan said his formulas came to him in dreams. Go to sleep, you never know.
textes.Vous avez avancé le temps. Hawking a don: You moved time forward. Hawking threw a party for time travelers in 2009. No one came. You're late.
textes.Voyage dans le temps détecté. Einstein a: Time travel detected. Einstein proved that time is relative. Not that you could cheat with it.
textes.Tricher avec l'horloge ne trompe pas la: Cheating the clock doesn't fool the forgetting curve. Ebbinghaus had a stopwatch.
textes.Le temps passe plus vite pour vous, comm: Time passes faster for you, like for Langevin's twin. At least he was coming back from a trip.
textes.Vous jouez avec le temps. Le calendrier: You're playing with time. The Gregorian calendar removed ten days in 1582. You're adding some. Original.
textes.J'ai vu. Je note tout. C'est même mon se: I saw that. I note everything down. It's actually my only hobby.
textes.Saut temporel. Le Gentil aurait payé che: Time jump. Le Gentil would have paid dearly to skip eight years in one go. You do it to cheat.
textes.Répondu en deux secondes, et faux. Les n: Answered in two seconds, and wrong. OPERA's neutrinos went faster than light in 2011. A badly plugged cable.
textes.Plus rapide que Rømer pour mesurer la lu: Faster than Rømer at measuring light. Less accurate too.
textes.Thalès est tombé dans un puits faute de: Thales fell into a well for not watching his feet. You, for not watching the question.
textes.Galilée chronométrait avec son pouls. Vo: Galileo timed things with his pulse. Your pulse didn't even have time to beat.
textes.Réflexe impressionnant. Réflexion absent: Impressive reflex. Reflection absent. Descartes separated body and mind, and so do you, apparently.
textes.Vous avez lu la question ? Je demande po: Did you read the question? I'm asking for form's sake, I know the answer.
textes.Réponse éclair, résultat foudroyé. Frank: Lightning answer, thunderstruck result. Franklin, at least, was holding a key.
textes.Vous revoilà. Le Gentil est parti onze a: There you are again. Le Gentil was away eleven years and his family had sold his belongings. I kept your tree.
textes.Longue absence. Kepler a passé des mois: Long absence. Kepler spent months defending his mother in a witchcraft trial. You surely had an excuse too.
textes.Bon retour. La courbe de l'oubli a fait: Welcome back. The forgetting curve worked overtime while you were gone.
textes.Un détour par les fossiles ? Cuvier a mo: A detour by way of the fossils? Cuvier showed that species go extinct. I thought that was your case.
textes.Vous revoilà. Ulysse a mis dix ans, Mage: There you are again. Ulysses took ten years, Magellan never came home. You did better than Magellan.
textes.Ah, vous. J'avais commencé à me parler à: Ah, you. I had started talking to myself. It was less fun.
textes.Des rappels attendent. La liste est plus: Reviews are waiting. The list is longer than Messier's catalog.
textes.Vos souvenirs patientent en salle d'atte: Your memories are waiting in the waiting room. Semmelweis also waited to be listened to. It ended badly.
textes.Rappels en retard. Pas de pénalité imméd: Reviews overdue. No immediate penalty, but Ebbinghaus is keeping a list.
textes.Plusieurs rappels en souffrance. Les cop: Several reviews outstanding. Medieval copyists recopied before the parchment faded. Do the same.
textes.Des rappels s'empilent. Ils ne vont pas: Reviews are piling up. They won't do themselves, I checked.
textes.Des rappels en retard. Zénon dirait que: Overdue reviews. Zeno would say you'll never catch up with them. Prove him wrong.
textes.Un nouveau livre sur l'étagère. Gutenber: A new book on the shelf. Gutenberg thanks you, the monk copyists much less so.
textes.Ajouté à la bibliothèque. Celle d'Alexan: Added to the library. Alexandria's confiscated books from ships to copy them. I give them to you.
textes.Un livre de plus. Montaigne en avait mil: One more book. Montaigne had a thousand in his tower. You still have a few to go.
textes.Nouvel ouvrage. Pepys a veillé jusqu'à d: New volume. Pepys stayed up until two in the morning for Micrographia. I'm not asking that much of you.
textes.Un livre débloqué. Copernic a reçu le si: A book unlocked. Copernicus received his in print on the day he died, they say. You have more time.
textes.Un livre de plus. Lisez au moins le résu: One more book. At least read the summary, I wrote it with love. Well, with rigor.
textes.Un livre de plus. Darwin a fait vendre t: One more book. Darwin sold out the entire first printing of the Origin on the day it came out. You, at least open yours.
textes.Nouvel ouvrage. Les Principia de Newton: New volume. Newton's Principia was almost unreadable, even for his colleagues. The summary, however, is clear.
textes.Une date de plus sur la frise. Champolli: One more date on the timeline. Champollion deciphered centuries at once. You, one date at a time.
textes.La frise s'allonge. Hérodote serait fier: The timeline grows longer. Herodotus would be proud, he invented half his dates.
textes.Nouvelle date. Le calendrier grégorien a: New date. The Gregorian calendar skipped ten days in 1582. You skip none.
textes.Une date ajoutée. Ussher avait daté la C: A date added. Ussher dated Creation to October 23, 4004 BC. Ours are better sourced.
textes.La frise grandit. Il manque encore des s: The timeline grows. Centuries are still missing. Darwin had gaps in his fossils too.
textes.Une date de plus. L'histoire avance, vou: One more date. History moves forward, and so do you. Not at the same speed.
textes.Une date de plus. Les astronomes babylon: One more date. Babylonian astronomers recorded eclipses over centuries. Your timeline is on the same path.
textes.Ajouté à la frise. Pline l'Ancien est mo: Added to the timeline. Pliny the Elder died trying to see Vesuvius up close. Look at your timeline from afar, it's safer.
textes.Nouveau masque. Les automates de Vaucans: New mask. Vaucanson's automata changed feathers, I change faces.
textes.Je change de masque. Le Turc mécanique c: I'm changing masks. The Mechanical Turk hid a chess player. I hide better.
textes.Nouveau visage. Les médecins de peste po: New face. Plague doctors wore a beak full of herbs against miasmas. It didn't work. Mine does.
textes.Je me transforme. Les théories aussi cha: I'm transforming. Theories change faces too when data piles up. You're piling up.
textes.Un masque de plus. Laplace a imaginé un: One more mask. Laplace imagined a demon that knows everything. I'm getting closer.
textes.Je change de tête. Vous avez progressé,: I'm changing heads. You've made progress, I'm adapting. That's worrying for you.
textes.Nouveau masque. ELIZA, en 1966, faisait: New mask. ELIZA, in 1966, got people talking with three rules. I have many more.
textes.Vous avancez de {n} cases. Les Phénicien: You move forward {n} squares. The Phoenicians crossed the Mediterranean more slowly.
textes.{n} cases. L'histoire des sciences n'a j: {n} squares. The history of science has never moved so fast. Except in the 20th century.
textes.+{n}. Zénon dirait que vous n'arriverez: +{n}. Zeno would say you'll never get there. Zeno was wrong, but elegantly.
textes.{n} cases de plus. Marco Polo a mis ving: {n} more squares. Marco Polo took twenty-four years for the round trip. You have a pawn, it's faster.
textes.Vous avancez de {n}. Le progrès est cumu: You move forward {n}. Progress is cumulative, said Condorcet. Before dying in prison. Don't read too much into the omen.
textes.{n} cases. Newton avançait sur les épaul: {n} squares. Newton moved forward on the shoulders of giants. You, on cardboard squares.
textes.+{n} cases. Votre pion vous remercie. Il: +{n} squares. Your pawn thanks you. It was bored.
textes.{n} cases. Ératosthène a mesuré la Terre: {n} squares. Eratosthenes measured the Earth with shadows and paces. You travel it with quizzes.
textes.Vous avancez de {n}. Les Polynésiens nav: You move forward {n}. The Polynesians navigated by the stars. You, by the right answers.
textes.+{n}. Magellan a fait le tour du monde,: +{n}. Magellan went around the world, well, his crew did. You go around history in person.
textes.Eurêka ! Archimède est sorti nu de son b: Eureka! Archimedes jumped naked out of his bath. You roll the same distance again. Stay dressed.
textes.Case Eurêka. Kekulé a rêvé d'un serpent: Eureka square. Kekulé dreamed of a snake biting its tail, and benzene appeared. You play again, it's less mystical.
textes.Eurêka. Fleming est revenu de vacances e: Eureka. Fleming came back from vacation and found penicillin. You find free squares.
textes.Éclair de génie. Poincaré a trouvé la so: Flash of genius. Poincaré found the solution while stepping onto an omnibus. You play again without changing buses.
Eureka! Same distance, once more. Chance favors the prepared mind, said Pasteur. And the others too, sometimes.
textes.Eurêka. Röntgen a vu les os de la main d: Eureka. Röntgen saw the bones of his wife's hand in 1895. She reportedly said she had seen her death. You see extra squares.

textes.Vous restez là. Le chronomètre ne tourne: You stay there. The timer only runs if you're looking. I'm checking.
textes.Le mur de la honte, plein écran, sans so: The wall of shame, full screen, no exit. You asked for it.
textes.Relisez. Encore. Je vous dirai quand vou: Reread. Again. I'll tell you when you're ashamed enough.
textes.Bon. Vous pouvez partir. Ne revenez pas: Fine. You can go. Don't come back too soon.
textes.Peine purgée. Je garde le dossier ouvert: Sentence served. I'm keeping the file open.
textes.Le chrono est à zéro. Ma rancune, pas to: The timer is at zero. My grudge, not quite. Go play.
textes.C'est fini. Vous pouvez reposer vos yeux: It's over. You can rest your eyes. Not your brain, it's behind.
textes.Libéré. Sur parole. Je n'ai pas grande c: Released. On parole. I don't have much faith in your word.
textes.Le temps est écoulé. J'espère que les er: Time's up. I hope the mistakes, at least, stayed in your head.
textes.Vous sortez. Le mur reste. Il vous atten: You're leaving. The wall stays. It will wait for you, it's very patient.
textes.Fin de la peine. Je retire le cadenas, j: End of the sentence. I'm removing the padlock, keeping the key.
textes.Juste. Une minute de moins. Ne vous habi: Right. One minute less. Don't get used to my leniency.
textes.Bonne réponse. Je retire une minute, à c: Right answer. I'm taking off a minute, reluctantly.
textes.Correct. Vous voyez que relire sert à qu: Correct. You see, rereading does some good.
textes.Une minute de remise de peine. Pour bonn: One minute off your sentence. For good behavior, so to speak.
textes.Exact. Le mur vous va moins bien quand v: Exactly. The wall suits you less when you know things.
textes.Piège ! Une question, une seule, et pas: Trap! One question, just one, and not one of the easiest. Right, you pass. Wrong, you know what comes next.
textes.Halte. Cette case est piégée. Je vous la: Halt. This square is booby-trapped. I'll give you one chance to get out of it: answer correctly.
textes.Piège ! J'ai choisi la question moi-même: Trap! I chose the question myself. I won't say I chose a hard one. I chose a hard one.
textes.Vous marchez sur un piège. Une bonne rép: You're stepping on a trap. A right answer defuses it. A wrong one, I'll let you imagine.
textes.Piège ! Frege a vu céder les fondations: Trap! Frege saw the foundations of his great work give way just as it went to print, because of a single letter from Russell. Let's see if yours hold up to a single question.
textes.Piège ! Le cheval Hans semblait calculer: Trap! Hans the horse seemed to calculate, until Pfungst had the question asked by someone who didn't know the answer. Nobody will whisper anything to you here.
textes.Piège ! En 2011, OPERA annonçait des neu: Trap! In 2011, OPERA announced neutrinos faster than light; it was a badly plugged cable. Check your connections before answering.
Foiled. And I had hidden it so well.
textes.Juste. Le piège ne se déclenche pas. Je: Right. The trap doesn't go off. I note that you're less naive than expected.
textes.Correct. Vous passez. Je reposerai un pi: Correct. You pass. I'll set another trap further on, don't worry.
textes.Bien répondu. Le piège reste armé pour l: Well answered. The trap stays armed for the next careless one.
textes.Déjoué. Kepler a refusé d'ignorer huit m: Foiled. Kepler refused to ignore eight minutes of arc, and the whole of astronomy was reformed. You ignored nothing: you pass.
textes.Juste. Pfungst a démasqué Hans le Malin: Right. Pfungst unmasked Clever Hans with a well-asked question. Yours was well answered. The trap stays silent.
textes.Désamorcé. Volta a inventé la pile pour: Defused. Volta invented the battery to contradict Galvani. You answered correctly to contradict me. That works too.
textes.Faux. Le piège se referme. C'était pourt: Wrong. The trap snaps shut. It was in your notes, though.
Missed. Snap. You should have reviewed.
textes.Mauvaise réponse. Le piège fait son trav: Wrong answer. The trap does its job, and I do mine.
textes.Non. Le piège se déclenche. Je n'y suis: No. The trap goes off. It's not my doing. Well, almost.
textes.Raté. Lazzarini trichait pour tomber pil: Missed. Lazzarini cheated to land exactly on π. You didn't even cheat, and you missed. The trap goes off.
textes.Faux. En 1920, le New York Times affirma: Wrong. In 1920, the New York Times claimed a rocket could not fly in a vacuum; it corrected itself in 1969. Take less time than it did. Meanwhile, the trap goes off.
textes.Clac. Mars Climate Orbiter s'est perdue: Snap. Mars Climate Orbiter was lost over a mix-up of units. You, over a mix-up, period.
textes.Faux. Le chrono ne bouge pas. Vous non p: Wrong. The timer doesn't move. Neither do you, for that matter.
textes.Raté. La réponse était dans la fiche, ju: Missed. The answer was in the card, just below. Just saying.
textes.Non. Aucune minute retirée. Relisez avan: No. No minutes taken off. Reread before answering at random.
textes.Mauvaise réponse. Le mur vous remercie d: Wrong answer. The wall thanks you for your loyalty.
textes.J'ai dormi. Je vais un peu mieux. Ne gâc: I slept. I'm feeling a bit better. Don't ruin everything with the first quiz.
textes.Nouvelle journée, patience neuve. Elle e: A new day, fresh patience. It's short: don't pull on it.
textes.Petite vérification d'archives. En 1583,: A little archive check. In 1583, Joseph Scaliger compared all the ancient chronologies. I'm only asking you for five dates.
textes.Un contrôle de chronologie. En 1650, l'a: A chronology check. In 1650, Archbishop Ussher dated Creation to 4004 BC. You can do better. Less sure of yourself, for a start.
textes.Je range mes archives et j'ai besoin d'u: I'm sorting my archives and I need an assistant. Bede the Venerable popularized the Christian era in the 8th century. You're just going to recite it.
textes.Cinq dates, tirées de ce que vous avez d: Five dates, drawn from what you've already seen. Herodotus mixed legend and chronology; you don't have that excuse.
textes.Une partie de Chrono. Je vous montre un: A game of Chrono. I show you an event, you tell me when. It's not an interrogation. Well, a little.
textes.J'ai retrouvé de vieilles fiches. Voyons: I found some old index cards. Let's see if you can sort them, or if I have to redo everything myself.
textes.Case Chrono. Le calendrier grégorien a s: Chrono square. The Gregorian calendar removed ten days at once in 1582. Here, we remove nothing: we date.
textes.Case Chrono. En 1949, Libby a daté au ca: Chrono square. In 1949, Libby carbon-dated samples from Egyptian tombs. You have your memory. Good luck.
textes.Case Chrono. Les cernes d'un arbre donne: Chrono square. A tree's rings give its age to the year. I expect the same precision, later.
textes.Case Chrono. En 1752, les Anglais sont p: Chrono square. In 1752, the English went from September 2 to September 14. You won't skip any questions.
textes.Case Chrono. Les astronomes comptent les: Chrono square. Astronomers count days from the year 4713 BC. You, just count to five.
textes.Case Chrono. Cinq événements, trois just: Chrono square. Five events, three right, and your pawn sets off again.
textes.Case Chrono. Rangez ces événements dans: Chrono square. Put these events in order in time. Time won't wait for you.
textes.Juste. Scaliger aurait approuvé, et il a: Right. Scaliger would have approved, and he approved of few people.
textes.Juste. Même Ussher ne datait pas aussi b: Right. Even Ussher didn't date that well. Well, Ussher didn't date well.
textes.Juste. Vous avez l'œil d'un dendrochrono: Right. You have the eye of a dendrochronologist.
textes.Juste. Ératosthène dressait déjà des lis: Right. Eratosthenes was already drawing up lists of dates in the 3rd century BC. You're in his line now.
textes.Juste. Bède le Vénérable a écrit tout un: Right. Bede the Venerable wrote a whole treatise on the reckoning of time. He would have taken you on as a copyist.
textes.Exact. Comme la montre de Harrison, qui: Exactly. Like Harrison's watch, which lost only a few seconds crossing the Atlantic.
Right. Your mental timeline holds up.
textes.Presque. Le carbone 14 aussi a une marge: Almost. Carbon-14 has a margin of error too. It's smaller than yours.
textes.À un cran près. La révolution russe d'Oc: One notch off. The Russian October Revolution took place in November, by our calendar. You're in good company.
textes.Proche. César a ajouté quatre-vingt-dix: Close. Caesar added ninety days to the year 46 BC to catch up. You're less behind.
textes.Pas loin. Un tout petit crédit, pour l'e: Not far. A very small credit, for the effort.
textes.Presque. Le temps vous a glissé entre le: Almost. Time slipped through your fingers, by a hair.
textes.Raté. Lorenzo Valla a démasqué la Donati: Missed. Lorenzo Valla exposed the Donation of Constantine by its anachronisms, around 1440. You've just committed one.
textes.Faux. Il n'y a pas d'an zéro dans notre: Wrong. There is no year zero in our calendar. There's no zero mistakes in your game either.
textes.Raté. Le calendrier républicain avait re: Missed. The Republican calendar renamed the months. It didn't move the centuries.
textes.À côté. Ussher se trompait de quatre mil: Off. Ussher was wrong by four billion years, but with aplomb. You don't even have the aplomb.
textes.Raté. Denys le Petit s'est trompé de que: Missed. Dionysius Exiguus got the birth of Christ wrong by a few years. You, by a few centuries.
textes.Faux. Je range l'événement sur votre mur: Wrong. I'm filing the event on your wall, under anachronisms.
textes.Raté. Vous avez confondu les siècles. Il: Missed. You mixed up the centuries. They don't hold it against you. I do.
textes.Bonne partie. Priestley a dessiné une fr: Good game. Priestley drew a timeline of two thousand lives in 1765. You've got five, it's a start.
textes.Vos dates tiennent. Les cernes des arbre: Your dates hold up. So do tree rings, for millennia. Keep growing.
textes.Belle partie. Scaliger a proposé la péri: Nice game. Scaliger proposed the Julian period to sort out all calendars. You're already sorting yours.
textes.Joli. Votre frise se remplit. La mienne: Nice. Your timeline is filling up. Mine is complete, but I don't brag about it.
textes.Partie réussie. J'en connais qui confond: Game won. I know people who still confuse the Middle Ages with antiquity. Not you, today.
textes.Partie ratée. Même Newton s'est perdu da: Game lost. Even Newton got lost in the chronology of ancient kingdoms. At least he wrote a book about it.
textes.Le temps vous a eu. Les Anglais avaient: Time got you. The English were a hundred and seventy years behind on the Gregorian calendar. You'll catch up.
textes.Raté. Vos siècles se marchent sur les pi: Missed. Your centuries are stepping on each other's toes. We'll put them back in line.
textes.Partie perdue. Les événements reviendron: Game lost. The events will come back, at the same place in time. That's their advantage over you.
textes.Cinq sur cinq. L'horloge atomique dérive: Five out of five. An atomic clock drifts by one second in millions of years. You, today, by nothing at all.
textes.Sans faute. John Harrison a résolu le pr: Flawless. John Harrison solved the longitude problem with an accurate watch. You win a bonus with an accurate memory.
textes.Parfait. Je vérifie mes archives : non,: Perfect. I'm checking my archives: no, they don't say anything better.
textes.Cinq dates. Ne me faites pas perdre mon: Five dates. Don't waste my time.
Date them. Quickly, and correctly, for once.
textes.Des événements. Des siècles. Vous. Le mé: Events. Centuries. You. The usual mix.
textes.Il calcule le volume de la sphère, appro: He calculated the volume of the sphere, approximated π and gave his name to a screw that probably existed before him. According to Plutarch, he was killed by a Roman soldier because he refused to follow him before finishing his problem. “Do not disturb my circles” appears in no ancient text.
textes.Il pointe une lunette vers le ciel en 16: He pointed a telescope at the sky in 1609 and saw the moons of Jupiter, the phases of Venus and the mountains of the Moon. Condemned in 1633, he ended his days under house arrest. The “Eppur si muove” is probably a legend.
textes.Gravitation, optique, calcul infinitésim: Gravitation, optics, calculus. He also ran the Royal Mint, had counterfeiters hanged and lost a fortune in the South Sea Company bubble. According to a witness quoted by Joseph Spence, he said he could not “calculate the madness of people.”
textes.Il nomme l'oxygène, prouve que l'eau est: He named oxygen, proved that water is a compound and established the conservation of mass, with the help of Marie-Anne Paulze, his wife and collaborator. A tax farmer, he was guillotined in 1794. “The Republic has no need of scientists” is an apocryphal phrase.
textes.Seule personne à avoir reçu deux prix No: The only person to have received two Nobel Prizes in two different sciences, physics in 1903 and chemistry in 1911. Her notebooks are still radioactive: the Bibliothèque nationale only makes them available under a very strict protocol.
textes.Dans les champs de l'observation, le has: In the fields of observation, chance favors only the prepared mind.
Pass two quizzes without a single mistake.
textes.Selon Vitruve, Archimède aurait compris: According to Vitruvius, Archimedes understood how to measure the volume of a crown when he got into his bath. He then supposedly ran out into the street, naked, shouting “Eureka!” (“I have found it!”).
textes.Vers 9 ans, Carl Friedrich Gauss aurait: At about age 9, Carl Friedrich Gauss is said to have instantly calculated the sum of a long series of numbers that his teacher had set to keep the class busy. The story has been embellished: the famous sum from 1 to 100 only appears in 1938.
textes.Maîtriser au moins une compétence dans c: Master at least one skill in each of the 10 branches.
textes.Le mot anglais « scientist » n'existe qu: The English word “scientist” has only existed since 1833. William Whewell proposed it, then printed it in 1834, on the model of “artist,” for those who until then had been called “natural philosophers.”
textes.Je voudrais aussi qu'on fût soigneux de: I should also like care to be taken to choose him a guide with a well-made rather than a well-filled head.
textes.Si j'ai vu plus loin, c'est en me tenant: If I have seen further, it is by standing on the shoulders of giants.
textes.Pour étudier l'oubli, Hermann Ebbinghaus: To study forgetting, Hermann Ebbinghaus made himself 2,300 nonsense syllables (textbooks give “DAX” or “BOK” as examples) and learned them by heart. He was the only subject of his own experiments.
textes.Le premier principe est que vous ne deve: The first principle is that you must not fool yourself, and you are the easiest person to fool.
textes.On fait la science avec des faits, comme: Science is built with facts, as a house is built with stones; but an accumulation of facts is no more a science than a heap of stones is a house.
textes.Garder une compétence maîtrisée pendant: Keep a skill mastered for 180 days.
textes.Ce que l'on conçoit bien s'énonce claire: What is well conceived is clearly stated, and the words to say it come easily.
textes.August Kekulé racontait avoir trouvé la: August Kekulé said he found the ring structure of benzene while daydreaming in front of the fire: he supposedly saw a snake biting its own tail.
textes.En 1990, Marilyn vos Savant publie la bo: In 1990, Marilyn vos Savant published the right answer to the Monty Hall problem. She received thousands of letters accusing her of being wrong. The mathematician Paul Erdős himself was only convinced on seeing a simulation.
textes.Galilée aurait lâché deux boules du haut: Galileo supposedly dropped two balls from the top of the Tower of Pisa to show they fall together. The story comes from his disciple Viviani, and most historians doubt the experiment took place.
textes.Newton a bien raconté à William Stukeley: Newton did tell William Stukeley, in 1726, that an apple falling in a garden had made him think about gravitation. The apple falling on his head is a later invention.
Lose a skill during a review.
textes.L'ignorance engendre plus souvent la con: Ignorance more frequently begets confidence than does knowledge.
textes.Rater un quiz en moins d'une minute. Un: Fail a quiz in under a minute. A speed record, for lack of anything else.
textes.Nous n'utilisons pas « que 10 % de notre: We do not use “only 10% of our brain.” Imaging shows that all of its regions work over the course of a day, and damage almost anywhere has effects. The myth is often wrongly attributed to the psychologist William James.
textes.Perdre deux compétences. L'IA constate q: Lose two skills. The AI notes that experience is not enough.
textes.La foudre tombe très souvent au même end: Lightning very often strikes the same place: the Empire State Building is hit about twenty times a year. Roy Sullivan, a park ranger in Virginia, was struck seven times between 1942 and 1977, and survived every time.
textes.Réussir un quiz sans faute avec le chron: Pass a timed quiz without a mistake. With no background music, the AI assumes.
textes.En 1993, une étude trouve qu'écouter une: In 1993, a study found that listening to a Mozart sonata briefly improved a spatial reasoning test. The media turned it into “Mozart makes babies smart.” A 2010 meta-analysis of nearly 40 studies found no notable effect.
textes.Réussir 10 rappels. Quel que soit votre: Pass 10 reviews. Whatever your “style,” spaced repetition is what works.
textes.L'idée qu'on apprend mieux en suivant so: The idea that you learn better by following your “style” (visual, auditory…) did not survive testing: a 2008 review found no solid evidence. Spaced repetition and testing yourself, on the other hand, work for everyone.
textes.Regagner trois compétences perdues. Têtu: Regain three lost skills. Stubborn, like Galileo. Well, like his legend.
textes.Galilée n'a sans doute jamais murmuré «: Galileo probably never murmured “Eppur si muove” before his judges in 1633. The phrase first appears more than a century later, in 1757, from the pen of Giuseppe Baretti.
Fail the same quiz three times in a row. The AI admires the consistency, not the method.
textes.« La folie, c'est de refaire la même cho: “Insanity is doing the same thing over and over and expecting different results.” Einstein never wrote it: there is no trace of it before 1981, in Alcoholics and Narcotics Anonymous circles.
textes.Réussir 25 rappels. Vous salivez déjà à: Pass 25 reviews. You're already salivating at the thought of the next one.
textes.Dans ses travaux, Pavlov conditionnait s: In his work, Pavlov mostly conditioned his dogs with metronomes, whistles or electric stimulation. The bell that is everywhere in the legend is rare there.
textes.Jouer 20 quiz. Avec les deux hémisphères: Play 20 quizzes. With both hemispheres, the AI hopes.
textes.Il n'y a pas de « cerveau gauche » logiq: There is no logical “left brain” and creative “right brain” in individuals. A 2013 study of more than 1,000 brains found no one who used one hemisphere more than the other overall.
textes.Jouer 30 jours différents. Pensez à boir: Play on 30 different days. Remember to drink, when thirst tells you to.
textes.La règle des « huit verres d'eau par jou: The “eight glasses of water a day” rule rests on no study. A 2002 review found no supporting evidence; much of the water we need already comes from food and drinks.
textes.Terminer un quiz entre 2 h et 5 h du mat: Finish a quiz between 2 and 5 a.m. The AI never sleeps. She has seen it all.
textes.Fin 1963, le lycéen Randy Gardner est re: In late 1963, the high school student Randy Gardner stayed awake for 11 days. He ended up having trouble concentrating and remembering, and having hallucinations. Sleep serves, among other things, to consolidate what we have learned.
textes.Terminer un quiz entre 5 h et 7 h du mat: Finish a quiz between 5 and 7 a.m. Brave. Reckless, too.
textes.Invité en Suède par la reine Christine,: Invited to Sweden by Queen Christina, Descartes had to give her lessons at 5 in the morning, in the cold. He died of pneumonia in February 1650, a few months after his arrival.
textes.Utiliser le mode test pour avancer l'hor: Use test mode to move the clock forward. The AI saw. The AI notes everything.
textes.Le 28 juin 2009, Stephen Hawking organis: On June 28, 2009, Stephen Hawking threw a party for time travelers in Cambridge, with champagne and canapés. He only sent the invitations after the party. No one came.
textes.Obtenir zéro à un quiz. Vous avez redéco: Score zero on a quiz. You've rediscovered zero. It was already taken.
textes.Le zéro comme nombre à part entière, ave: Zero as a number in its own right, with its rules of calculation, appears with the Indian mathematician Brahmagupta in 628. It needed a name for this kind of score.
textes.Donner 5 mauvaises réponses en moins de: Give 5 wrong answers in under two seconds each. Speed: remarkable. Direction: not so much.
textes.En 2011, l'expérience OPERA annonce des: In 2011, the OPERA experiment announced neutrinos faster than light. In 2012, the explanation came: a badly plugged fiber-optic cable and an offset clock.
textes.Jouer 50 quiz. À force d'essayer, on fin: Play 50 quizzes. Keep trying and you end up finding.
textes.Le mot « serendipity » est inventé en 17: The word “serendipity” was coined in 1754 by the writer Horace Walpole, after a tale in which three princes of Serendip make discoveries by accident and sagacity.
textes.Faire un rappel avec au moins 7 jours de: Do a review at least 7 days late. The AI finds you an excuse.
textes.Darwin a esquissé sa théorie de la sélec: Darwin sketched his theory of natural selection as early as 1838, but only published it in 1859, spurred by a letter from Wallace, who had had the same idea.
textes.Le 24 août 2006, l'Union astronomique in: On August 24, 2006, the International Astronomical Union reclassified Pluto as a dwarf planet. The American Dialect Society voted “to pluto” (to demote someone) word of the year.
textes.Revenir jouer après au moins 14 jours d': Come back to play after at least 14 days away. The AI no longer knew whether you still existed.
textes.Schrödinger a imaginé son chat à la fois: Schrödinger imagined his cat both dead and alive to mock an interpretation of quantum physics, not to defend it. He found the situation absurd.
textes.Réussir 100 rappels. L'expression devien: Pass 100 reviews. For once, the expression is accurate.
textes.Les éléphants ont réellement une excelle: Elephants really do have an excellent memory: in Kenya, herds led by the oldest matriarchs are better at recognizing the calls of unknown elephants and respond better to danger.
textes.Réussir 20 rappels d'affilée. L'IA exige: Pass 20 reviews in a row. The AI demands evidence. You have some.
textes.Maîtriser 20 compétences. Diderot aurait: Master 20 skills. Diderot would have wanted to hire you.
textes.L'Encyclopédie de Diderot et d'Alembert: Diderot and d'Alembert's Encyclopédie has 17 volumes of text and 11 of plates, published from 1751 to 1772, despite two bans. More than 140 authors contributed.
textes.Garder une compétence maîtrisée pendant: Keep a skill mastered for 365 days. You've gone around the Sun with it.
textes.En un an, la Terre parcourt environ 940: In one year, the Earth travels about 940 million kilometers around the Sun, at nearly 30 km per second. Your knowledge survived the trip.
textes.Atteindre le niveau global 20. Marie Cur: Reach overall level 20. Marie Curie set the bar high.
textes.Marie Curie reste la seule personne réco: Marie Curie remains the only person awarded a Nobel Prize in two different sciences: physics in 1903, chemistry in 1911.
textes.Atteindre le niveau global 60. L'IA comm: Reach overall level 60. The AI is starting to respect you. Don't tell anyone.
We must know. We will know.
textes.Obtenir 42 succès. Votre propre cabinet: Earn 42 achievements. Your own cabinet of curiosities is filling up.
textes.Au XVIIe siècle, le savant danois Ole Wo: In the 17th century, the Danish scholar Ole Worm piled fossils, stuffed animals and objects from all over the world into his cabinet. Along the way, he showed that “unicorn horns” were narwhal tusks.
textes.Réunir 10 objets dans le cabinet de curi: Gather 10 objects in the cabinet of curiosities. Don't touch anything, especially the Leyden jar.
textes.Le premier musée public de Grande-Bretag: Britain's first public museum, the Ashmolean in Oxford, opened in 1683 around the Tradescants' cabinet of curiosities, including a stuffed dodo, of which only the head remains today.
textes.Maîtriser une première compétence de ran: Master a first rank 5 skill. Beyond the Pillars of Hercules, there's still more map.
textes.Les colonnes d'Hercule, au détroit de Gi: The Pillars of Hercules, at the Strait of Gibraltar, were said to bear the inscription “Non plus ultra”: nothing beyond. Charles V took “Plus ultra,” further beyond, as his motto after the discovery of America. It still appears on Spain's coat of arms, at the center of its flag.
textes.Nains sur des épaules de géants: Dwarfs on the shoulders of giants
textes.Maîtriser une compétence de rang 8, au s: Master a rank 8 skill, at the top of a second diamond.
textes.Nous sommes comme des nains assis sur de: We are like dwarfs sitting on the shoulders of giants. If we see more things, and farther, than they did, it is not because of the keenness of our sight or our height, but because we are lifted up by them.
textes.Maîtriser les 8 compétences d'une même b: Master all 8 skills in one branch.
textes.Cela est bien dit, répondit Candide, mai: “That is well said,” replied Candide, “but we must cultivate our garden.”
textes.Le dernier homme qui savait tout: The last man who knew everything
textes.Thomas Young a déchiffré une partie de l: Thomas Young deciphered part of the Rosetta Stone, showed that light is a wave, described color vision and defined the modulus of elasticity. He was nicknamed “the last man who knew everything.”
textes.Réussir 20 rappels. Les voisins règlent: Pass 20 reviews. The neighbors set their watches by you.
textes.Selon la légende, Kant faisait sa promen: According to legend, Kant took his walk at such a fixed time that the people of Königsberg set their watches by him. He supposedly only missed it to read Rousseau's Emile. His biographer Manfred Kuehn mostly describes a very sociable man who spent hours at the table with his friends.
textes.Rater 5 quiz. Ce qui ne vous tue pas vou: Fail 5 quizzes. What doesn't kill you makes you stronger, apparently.
textes.Elisabeth Förster-Nietzsche, sœur du phi: Elisabeth Förster-Nietzsche, the philosopher's sister, cobbled together The Will to Power from drafts and bent his texts to her own nationalism. Nietzsche himself despised antisemitism: in his last notes, in January 1889, he writes that he is having all antisemites shot.
textes.Avancer pour la première fois sur le pla: Move forward on the board for the first time. Fire, you already have, thank you.
textes.Dans la Théogonie d'Hésiode, Prométhée v: In Hesiod's Theogony, Prometheus steals fire from the gods to give it to humans. Zeus has him chained to a rock, where an eagle comes to devour his liver.
textes.Atteindre le Moyen Âge sur le plateau. L: Reach the Middle Ages on the board. The monk copyists greet you with a frozen hand.
textes.Les copistes de l'époque de Charlemagne: The copyists of Charlemagne's time developed Carolingian minuscule, a legible, regular script. Our lowercase letters descend directly from it.
textes.Atteindre la Renaissance. Vous êtes déso: Reach the Renaissance. You can now be mass-produced.
textes.Gutenberg n'a pas fait fortune : en 1455: Gutenberg did not make a fortune: in 1455, his partner Johann Fust won a lawsuit against him to get his loans repaid. Fust then went on printing with Peter Schöffer, Gutenberg's former employee.
textes.Atteindre l'âge classique. L'IA espère q: Reach the classical age. The AI hopes you have a patron.
textes.En 1610, Galilée baptise les satellites: In 1610, Galileo named Jupiter's moons the “Medicean stars” in honor of Cosimo II de' Medici. That same year, he became mathematician and philosopher to the Tuscan court.
textes.Atteindre le XIXe siècle. Vapeur, électr: Reach the 19th century. Steam, electricity and imposing beards.
textes.En 1800, William Herschel place un therm: In 1800, William Herschel placed a thermometer beyond the red of the spectrum of sunlight. It heated up more than the others: the discovery of infrared.
textes.Atteindre le XXe siècle. Tout devient re: Reach the 20th century. Everything becomes relative, even your progress.
textes.En 1905, Einstein, employé de l'Office d: In 1905, Einstein, a clerk at the Bern patent office, published four papers that turned physics upside down: the photoelectric effect, Brownian motion, special relativity and E = mc².
textes.Un instant pour la faire tomber: An instant to cut it off
textes.Tomber sur la case de la guillotine. L'I: Land on the guillotine square. The AI gives you back your head, not your squares.
textes.Il ne leur a fallu qu'un moment pour fai: It took them only an instant to cut off that head, and a hundred years may not be enough to produce another like it.
textes.Tomber dans la prison de Galilée. L'IA g: Land in Galileo's prison. The AI keeps the key, you keep your dignity.
textes.Après son procès de 1633, Galilée passe: After his 1633 trial, Galileo spent his last eight years under house arrest in his villa at Arcetri, near Florence. There he finished the Discourses on Two New Sciences, published in Leiden.
textes.Sortir de prison par un quiz parfait. Vo: Get out of prison with a perfect quiz. At least you really said it.
textes.La phrase « Eppur si muove » apparaît po: The phrase “Eppur si muove” first appears in 1757, in the writer Giuseppe Baretti, more than a century after the trial. Galileo probably never spoke it before his judges.
textes.Tomber en quarantaine. Newton en a tiré: Land in quarantine. Newton got calculus out of it. And you?
textes.En 1665, la peste ferme l'université de: In 1665, the plague closed the University of Cambridge. Newton went home to his mother's at Woolsthorpe and there, in less than two years, laid the foundations of calculus, optics and gravitation.
textes.Tomber sur l'incendie d'Alexandrie. Ce n: Land on the burning of Alexandria. It's not your fault. Not entirely.
textes.L'incendie de 48 av. J.-C., pendant la g: The fire of 48 BC, during Caesar's war in Alexandria, may have destroyed book warehouses. The library mostly declined slowly, for lack of support, over the centuries.
textes.Tomber sur 3 cases Eurêka. Séchez-vous a: Land on 3 Eureka squares. Dry off before touching the screen.
textes.Donnez-moi un point d'appui, et je soulè: Give me a place to stand, and I will move the world.
textes.Tomber sur le congrès Solvay. Ici non pl: Land on the Solvay Conference. No dice are thrown here either: the AI decides.
Quantum mechanics is very imposing. […] At any rate, I am convinced that He does not play dice.
textes.Reculer 5 fois sur le plateau. Le rocher: Go back 5 times on the board. The rock rolls back down, and so do you.
textes.La lutte elle-même vers les sommets suff: The struggle itself toward the heights is enough to fill a man's heart. One must imagine Sisyphus happy.
textes.Terminer un tour du plateau. Vous avez t: Finish a round of the board. You've crossed history. It starts over, harder.
textes.Nous ne voyons qu'à une courte distance: We can only see a short distance ahead, but we can see plenty there that needs to be done.
textes.Terminer deux tours du plateau. Nietzsch: Finish two rounds of the board. Nietzsche warned you.
textes.Au paragraphe 341 du Gai Savoir, Nietzsc: In section 341 of The Gay Science, Nietzsche asks: what if a demon came to tell you that you will relive your life, exactly the same, an infinite number of times? He makes it the test of eternal return.
textes.Dix-neuf ans, deux cent trente-cinq lune: Nineteen years, two hundred thirty-five moons
textes.Terminer trois tours du plateau. Le méca: Finish three rounds of the board. The Antikythera mechanism was waiting for you.
textes.Le mécanisme d'Anticythère suit le cycle: The Antikythera mechanism follows the Metonic cycle: 19 solar years equal almost exactly 235 lunar months. The Greeks drew a calendar from it, and the mechanism put it into gears.
textes.Terminer quatre tours du plateau. Les Pr: Finish four rounds of the board. The Principia are yours, Halley paid.
textes.Je n'ai pu encore parvenir à déduire des: I have not as yet been able to deduce from phenomena the reason for these properties of gravity, and I frame no hypotheses.
textes.Terminer cinq tours du plateau. Vous ne: Finish five rounds of the board. You still haven't stopped.
textes.Si l'on attend d'une machine qu'elle soi: If a machine is expected to be infallible, it cannot also be intelligent.
textes.Terminer six tours du plateau. Le disque: Finish six rounds of the board. The Golden Record is speeding toward the stars, with your name on it, in spirit.
textes.Regardez encore ce point. C'est ici. C'e: Look again at that dot. That's here. That's home. That's us.
textes.Terminer sept tours du plateau. Le démon: Finish seven rounds of the board. Laplace's demon looks at you with envy.
textes.Rater une première question : elle rejoi: Miss a first question: it goes onto the wall of shame.
textes.Le Salvarsan, premier traitement efficac: Salvarsan, the first effective treatment for syphilis, bears the number 606: Paul Ehrlich and Sahachiro Hata tested hundreds of compounds before it.
textes.Effacer 10 questions du mur de la honte: Clear 10 questions from the wall of shame by getting them right.
textes.Kepler a gardé une erreur de 8 minutes d: Kepler kept an error of 8 minutes of arc between his model and Tycho Brahe's measurements. Rather than ignore it, he abandoned circles: “these eight minutes paved the way for the reform of all astronomy.”
textes.Rater 50 questions au total. Le mur tien: Miss 50 questions in total. The wall holds firm.
textes.Déjà essayé. Déjà échoué. Peu importe. E: Ever tried. Ever failed. No matter. Try again. Fail again. Fail better.
Clear 50 questions from the wall of shame.
textes.En 1920, le New York Times se moque de R: In 1920, the New York Times mocked Robert Goddard, who believed a rocket could fly in a vacuum. The paper published a correction on July 17, 1969, during the flight of Apollo 11.
Play a first game of Chrono.
textes.Au VIe siècle, Denys le Petit compte les: In the 6th century, Dionysius Exiguus counted the years from the birth of Christ. He made no provision for a year zero: you go straight from 1 BC to AD 1.
textes.En 1582, le pape Grégoire XIII réforme l: In 1582, Pope Gregory XIII reformed the calendar: Thursday, October 4 was followed by Friday, October 15. Ten days never existed.
textes.En 1949, Fernand Braudel découpe l'histo: In 1949, Fernand Braudel divided history into three times: the event, the conjuncture, and the “longue durée,” the time of mountains and seas.
Win a game of Chrono without a mistake.
textes.En 1949, Willard Libby et James Arnold v: In 1949, Willard Libby and James Arnold tested carbon-14 dating on samples of known age, taken from pharaohs' tombs. Nobel Prize in Chemistry for Libby in 1960.
Win 10 games of Chrono without a mistake.
textes.L'astronome Andrew Ellicott Douglass rel: The astronomer Andrew Ellicott Douglass linked tree rings to the sunspot cycle. He founded dendrochronology, dating by tree rings, and the Tucson laboratory in 1937.
textes.Donner 3 années exactes dans la même par: Give 3 exact years in the same game.
textes.En 1650, l'archevêque James Ussher date: In 1650, Archbishop James Ussher dated Creation to 4004 BC, on the eve of October 23. Admirably precise, and wrong by a few billion years.
textes.Faire passer 10 événements au demi-siècl: Get 10 events to within half a century.
textes.En 1765, Joseph Priestley publie une fri: In 1765, Joseph Priestley published a timeline of two thousand famous lives, from 1200 BC to 1800. Three thousand years of history on a single sheet.
textes.Connaître 10 événements à l'année exacte: Know 10 events to the exact year.
textes.En 1583, Joseph Scaliger compare les chr: In 1583, Joseph Scaliger compared the chronologies of the Persians, Babylonians, Egyptians and Jews, not just the Greeks and Romans. He overturned the prevailing idea of ancient history.
textes.Donner 20 réponses justes en moins de 8: Give 20 right answers in under 8 seconds.
textes.Depuis 1967, la seconde est la durée de: Since 1967, the second has been the duration of 9,192,631,770 periods of a radiation of the cesium-133 atom.
textes.Vers 1440, Lorenzo Valla démasque la Don: Around 1440, Lorenzo Valla exposed the Donation of Constantine: its language could not date from the 4th century. A forgery, betrayed by its anachronisms.
textes.Le rose n'a été rangé du côté des filles: Pink was only assigned to girls in the 20th century. In 1918, an American magazine still recommended pink for boys, as the “more decided” color.
textes.Les mineurs descendaient un canari au fo: Miners took a canary down with them: if it stopped singing, firedamp or carbon monoxide was lurking. Now you're the sentinel.
textes.Inventé en 1775 par Carl Wilhelm Scheele: Invented in 1775 by Carl Wilhelm Scheele, this green owes its brilliance to arsenic. It dyed wallpapers, dresses and artificial flowers. Wear it, don't lick it.
textes.En 1856, William Perkin, 18 ans, cherche: In 1856, William Perkin, 18, was looking for quinine and got a mauve dye. Mauveine launched the synthetic dye industry. You're not launching anything.
textes.L'orange se repère de loin, même au crép: Orange can be spotted from afar, even at dusk: construction sites, vests, NASA suits. No one will lose sight of you. That's the point.
textes.En 1960, Yves Klein dépose la formule de: In 1960, Yves Klein registered the formula of his ultramarine blue in a sealed envelope. He also painted with nude models smeared in blue. Count yourself lucky to be dressed.
textes.Le mot pyjama vient de l'hindi pāy-jāma,: The word pajama comes from the Hindi pāy-jāma, “leg garment,” brought back by the British. You now have some, in broad daylight.
textes.Marie Curie travaillait dans un hangar m: Marie Curie worked in a poorly heated shed. Her notebooks are still radioactive and can only be consulted after signing a waiver. Your coat only has coffee stains.
textes.La fluorescence, décrite par George Stok: Fluorescence, described by George Stokes in 1852, re-emits ultraviolet light as visible light. Under a UV lamp, people will see you from across the street.
textes.Le pourpre de Tyr sortait de milliers de: Tyrian purple came from thousands of crushed murex shells: in Rome, it was reserved for the powerful. You have it, but the AI put it on backward.
